Awful service. No food choices, no welcome drinks, no menus and poor quality overall. Can't believe how bad the service has slipped and COVID can't be blamed for this issue. This is budget cutting at its worse, while still charging premium prices to passengers. We paid £600 to upgrade to premium from economy and it was the worst decision ever. Upper class were given everything from champagne to snacks to meal choices and the rest of the flight had to mop up the scraps. Not the fault of the crew as half the stock wasn't loaded by ground staff, and they were in the line of fire from several passengers. Felt bad for them but they said that this was a regular occurrence that they don't have the stock or items to give a top service. Come on virgin, get your act together and up your game - there are several other airlines to choose from and customers will go elsewhere for better service.

The seat is a lie-flat. But it is extremely narrow compared to competition and very worn out. Seat cushions also worn out, so no help for comfort. The possibility to store your personal items is very unpractical and nothing to store your glasses during the night. The dashboard to move the seat has no light so most unpractical at night. The electrical plug did work. The tray is pretty wide but only has 2 positions: up or down! impossible to get it closer to you when eating.

A330 Business class product is awful. Was no selection of food and was given a very bland pasta despite having a gluten intolerance. Cabin AC was faulty and stuck on lowest setting. Cabin crew did the best they could. Customer services response was pathetic.

I have been traveling for united airlines for many times, but they always have the most horrible service. Their customer service is very rude. I think that they very soon expect that the people pay for their services helping the people. I asked them about another seat because I am very tall and their answer was if you need to change your seat have to pay but in the middle.

Very unhappy. Booked a forward facing window seat well over a moth prior to the flight, and even when checking in online the night before that seat was showing as my reserved seat. After arriving at the airport my seat was changed. When asked they could only tell me there was no comment as to why my seat was changed. Now I’m riding backwards on the aisle and over the engine instead of being tucked away by the window and having a forward facing seat ahead of the noise of the engine. Incredibly disappointed and my next business trip will be through Dubai with a drive to Abu Dhabi. 4 stars because the crew was good and the food was good. But not getting what was paid for is pretty terrible. I personally hate the Etihad business configuration. The new United polaris is similar but is much better with no rear facing seats.

The seat is quite comfortable and has good legroom, there is good space on the window seats, the IFE is outdated though and you can't adjust the angle of the head rest. The window is very big and your receive some sort of service every 1-2 hrs.

My husband and I booked United from our trip back from Saudi Arabia. It was from Chicago to Minneapolis. They put us in two different seats. My husband asked the crew member to put us together. She was super rude and said now, he needs to sit where his seat is at. He said ok I will just wait for the person who’s placed next to my wife and I will ask to switch the seat. She replied no while rising her voice at him. She told him to seat where he’s scheduled to be. The person who was scheduled to seat next to my husband agreed to switch with us. We thanked him and I got to seat next to my husband. She came to the guy and was like sir you didn’t have to do, but I will give you points on your mileage or whatever she was talking about. Through out the trip which was 1 hr and 4 minutes to MSP she was loud and rude to us. We will never use United ever again.

We (2 passengers) had both a horrible experience with our seats deflating, so that we had a horizontal metal bar pushing hard against out mid thoracic spine on this 16 hour flight! Exactly the same happened on the return leg on different business class seat allocations. Each time the crew was trying hard to improve the situation with blankets, but it was still a painful experience. Business class was full, so no option to move seats. During the stopover in Vancouver a technical crew came on board, attended to my seat and showed me how to take the seat cover off and manually blow air into the seat with my mouth), which I had to do 3 times during the flight back from JFK after Vancouver. The business class seat is actually a really good product (on A350-900, same like Qantas) with air cushioned seat that should be adjustable, but the airline simply doesn’t maintain or repair it. It is such a shame, but it reflects the overall chaotic operation of this airline. On boarding the MEL-MNL (different business seats) leg I immediately noticed that my remote control was broken with exposed wires and it is only after I insisted that they put a sticker over the wires to conceal them (the plane was still on the ground in Melbourne). Seat on the MEL-MNL-MEL ok, but tiny footwells (A330-300). During each transit in Manila we had to wait for our suitcases to be found and open them for security inspection, almost missing our return flight back to Melbourne because they had difficulty finding our luggage. That is a normal procedure, when transiting in Manila. I’m not going to even go into the catering, other than to say that “they are trying”. IFE was mediocre. I have not received an answer to my complaint, despite repeated emails. To sum it up: Horrible airline, zero customer service! While the tickets seem cheaper compared to other airlines, they are in fact terrible value for money…

Delta One was my first choice before covid but this time the seat layout, size, angle gave me the worst experience. The leg space for window suit was way too small. At full flat position, I couldn’t turn my body because my feet are stuck in the leg space. I had to make seat upright first to turn my body. The full flat seat is tilted too much, so my body was tense whole flight. I had a backache when I arrived in Seoul, then after taking the inbound flight( this time at center suite) I had a little more legroom but seat was still too steep, i started having a muscle tenderness (couldn’t walk or wake up) for 1 full day after the flight. Food was worse than before but still acceptable for Coming back flight. The food prepared in Seattle was so bad. As an appetizer, I had a half cut egg roll, fried shrimp, both were tasteless. Food prepared in Korea was a tasty chicken salad. Never fly Delta One any longer.

Very poor experience flying with Air India. Most passengers in Economy Class had something wrong with their seat. In my row, on both my departing and returning flights, none of the three seats had a working screen. My seat did not recline either time. On my departing flight, my seat was missing it's bottom cushion, so I was sitting on a thin layer of padding over hard plastic. The food was very terrible. Given that it's Air India, they have a very limited number of non-vegetarian meals even though most of the passengers were non-vegetarian. So during all meals they were out of non-veg meals by the time they got to me. I generally like vegetarian food, but the food they served was honestly so terrible.

Was sat in the emergency exit row. Ample leg room but was a little tight with elbow room. Entertainment system was ok but would prefer a newer movie selection. Breakfast meal was a little heavy, but enjoyed the selection including fruit, yogurt and croissant. Service professional and courteous. Overall the flight was enjoyable
The seat was good and comfortable enough for 6 hours flight. The width is big enough for my body. The legroom is modest. Adjustable headrest well function. Lucky enough to occupy all three seats.

Did research, premium economy, looks good with extra width seats more legroom and extra recline on the seats. We had a 20 hour red eye flight LHR to SYD with a refuelling and quick crew change in SIN. Looks deceive. We were seated in row E (middle 2 of 4) centre aisle. Great, until the seat in front reclined and we discovered we were trapped. The seat arms are not retractable, (that is where the tray table is located). The distance between the arm rest and the fully reclined seat in front is under 7 inches. To extract yourself you have to wake 3 passengers, 2 in front to lift their seat backs to an upright position and the passenger to your side to allow you to lift your legs up over the arm rests. I found it impossible to watch my screen due to it being so far off vertical, it was sending me dizzy looking at it. One other problem I discovered, because I was stressed at being uncomfortable I started getting hot to find the Boeing 777 does not have individual air conditioning cold air nozzles, once the temperature is set it can’t be individually cooled. On the positive side the food was good I did however miss the coffee pot after the meal.

Seating is very uncomfortable.  Sleeping configuration is not comfortable. You need to sleep on an angle sticking your feet in a small hole. The seat is lightly padded. Food is low quality for business class and no longer offers a rich Peranakan mix, but a Chinese bias. Media system resets when any connected device detaches and reattaches. Book the chef food never got loaded.
My seat (71J) was terrible. There was 2 black boxes fixed under the seat before me leaving me only 60% of the space that my feet would have had if I had been sitting in different row.

Not the most comfortable seats in the class. The legroom is on the tight side, the seats are padded and soft. Cabin crew also gave us pillow and blanket to max out comfort for a short nap. Overall, there was nothing I can complain about. If you want extra comfort, go for some of the Middle East airlines.

We got a great deal on the Premium Economy class RT to AMS and back. We picked the bulkhead window seats and the legroom was excellent. However, the legrest is rather useless as it does not offer any improvement on the seat. The food and service were above average and superior to economy but certainly nothing close to the business class as we upgraded to BC on the outbound flight. I will certainly recommend KLM and its PE and BC seats

Rows squeezed in so tight that even as a 166cm short man who is not fat the tray table is touching my belly and I can’t even use it to write on without elbowing my neighbours. I don’t know how the tall man across the aisle from me is coping. We are also stuck on the tarmac waiting for the toilet holding tanks to be emptied. Been delayed half an hour already with no word on how long it will take to fix the problem (if we will depart at all). The seat pocket is too small for a drink bottle. I only flew Jetstar because it was cheap but I think I’ll stick to other airlines in future.

Not really comfortable chair or bed. Singapore Airlines offer a proper bed and a separate chair in First Suite: Both are rather disappointing, especially taken into account the huge investment and Publicity. The leather chair stands alone in the middle of the Suite, one has to move it from the take-off position, to the dining position, and to the outside view position. The bed is not facing the direction of travel, but crossways in the suite. The bed is narrow and very hard, not very comfortable. When the bed is not used, it hangs across the suite like a chunk of white painted wood. The whole design is not well thought through and not nicely done.

Recently, I reviewed a Business Class seat on an A350-900 whilst on a flight from BER to DOH. Today, I ended up on the same aircraft, but with a different seat layout. I reserved a window seat, but during checkin, I was just assigned a different seat in the middle bit of the row. I tried to change this at the airport, but was told, that it’s not possible. So, no QSuite, but a middle seat with a small divider to my neighbor. There was no privacy, the seat felt stuffy, there was not much legroom. Not a nice experience.

I tried the new A388 business class from London to Singapore. It was about 12-13 hours. My seat was 21K on the upper deck, along with the suites (the old ones used to be in the bottom deck). I think that the seat was pretty spacious for me (I'm 164cm) the footrest was good, but the legroom was to either to your left or right, which makes it quite uncomfortable. But on the SQ regional J class, its a straight legroom, so consider getting a 787-10/359 if you want a straight legroom. The bed couldn't recline fully into a flat bed, unlike the 773,359, the 388 uses buttons to recline the bed, it is done automatically, while the 773/359 is done manually. The table was pretty small compared to the 773/359 (hard to get out of your seat while the table is open) and some tables are also not fully functional, like mine, during landing the table popped back out, I have tried several times to push the table back in, but it just won't fully go in, it would still be loose. The crew was very kind, friendly and welcoming. They kept checking on me, which made me feel weird but happy in a way. I had 2 meals in total on this flight, lunch and supper/dinner. The lunch wasn't my favourite, the scrambled eggs were pretty basic. But the Dinner/supper, I love it, it was steak beef served with mash potatoes and a couple of vegetables, (not book the cook).

Air Canada has the worst economy seat of airlines I have flown. The seat was torturous on this 13.5 hour flight from Dubai to Toronto. The seats have a light construction with poor cushioning and a terrible lumbar support. The adjustable head rest was very uncomfortable. The seat material was abrasive and added to my discomfort. The seats had no front foot rest. While the recline was reasonable and perhaps considerate of passengers behind, some seats reclined more than others.
Very spacious and comfortable seats. I'm very tall and I felt that I had enough space during the whole journey. The screen was also standards and movies were good.

JAL Sky Suite III - reverse herringbone.  Tight space, claustrophobic and uncomfortable. It might work if you are a very small person but it's shocking for a long haul flight. Be aware that JAL has many different business class seat types on their B787 and this is the worst, though the latest. Skysuite II is vastly better and preferable, even though it is 2x2x2 but with staggered layout.

Hawaiian Airlines refers to their Premium Economy seats as Extra Comfort. The seats on the A-330 is 18 inches and the pitch is 36 inches. Even with my backpack under the seat in front of me I am able to be fairly comfortable, even at 5'11. The general comfort is adequate, not luxury. Padding on the sets is fine for the six hours and 45 minutes you spend on the plane from boarding to deplaning when flying from the west coast. I have never had a problem with the IFE, though the selection could use a little more updating. Each IFE screen has USB charging ports and there is universal power for the Extra Comfort seats.

Seats very narrow. There is not much arm or leg space, even for someone who are small. I selected 42A for outbound and 42K for inbound, both are window seats, close but not next to the lavatory. Can't say it is a good choice. Had to cross two people to get out of my seats. Both of them have to stand up at the aisle in order for me to get out. Any movement will Also, it's hard to recline the back of seat. Entertainment system is good, good selection of shows to watch.

If you are considering booking extra leg room seats on an Emirates flight don’t. While their normal seats are comfy with sufficient leg room regrettably the same cannot be said about their extra leg room seats. These are situated next to the toilets, the tv screen is in a section of the seat making them narrower than the regular seats and less comfy. The main problem is that the lights from the toilets do not dim and make it difficult to sleep. In addition the space in front of you “your extra leg room” is continually used by people queueing for the toilet. We would therefore advise that you stick to the normal seats and save yourself some money.

This seat is cramped. The pitch is 30-31 inches. The metal support from floor for seat in front is exactly in the space where you would naturally place your right leg, reducing the legroom significantly. I could not imagine siting in this seat for 12 hours, it would be torture. Luckily for me was a quick trip to Bangkok.

There are two configs on the A350, the 2x2x2 & the staggered seating. My preference is for the older seating it is less cramped. The seat/bed is comfortable. The meals are excellent especially the Ethiopian Cuisine. All the flights were on time and the service level on the aircraft exemplary. The Biz lounge at Addis is great, albeit a bit of a scrum 0700-1000 when all the transits/ transfers take place. I have used them twice on the UK -JNB route, better timings than EK or Qatar

BA doesn't seem to understand why its customers choose to fly with them over low-cost carriers like Ryanair, easyJet or Wizz Air and the keep racing to the bottom, despite never being cheap enough or comprehensive enough in terms of flights to certain destinations. They've installed the same appalling slimline seats easyJet and Wizz Air have, but managed to make them even more uncomfortable. They have no lumbar support, and also don't have headrests like BA's old Pinnacle seats. They also have no recline and despite being refurbished had no at seat charging either. My understanding was that seats upto row 12 should have the old Pinnacle seats, so I woke up early to check-in just as check-in opened on the app 24hrs before and was pleased to bag a seat in row 10 which should mean I have the old Pinnacle seat. Apparently not, at least not on BA Euroflyer their subsidiary at Gatwick, the whole plane had the new appalling slimline seats even in Business - I'd have been pretty appalled if I had paid extra to fly in that cabin and been left with that seat for 3hrs. They are probably ok for an 1 maybe 2hr flight max, but on a 3hr flight to Catania from Heathrow it was painful and we were left with a horrible back pain.
One of the worst business class seats, tiny seat. The lay out of the aircraft is very cramped, the plane was very dirty, amenity kit awful, service in general, not so good.

I had confirmed the seat suitable for my needs, had the seat confirmed with the boarding pass printed and issued to me. At the point of boarding I was told my seat was moved with no real reason given although we suspect it was to accommodate other passengers who do not seem to have any real reason to need to take over my seat. I ended up having to sit with the bad ear nearer to the aisle and could not hear what the flight attendant was saying. I am most displeased at this inconsiderate change without any prior discussion with me by the airline.
Spacious, clean and comfortable seat with outstanding IFE and food served. Excellent amenities and blankets/pillows. Qsuite with privacy and lots of legroom with easy to use seat controls.

We booked business class for our flight to and from New York. We fly business class a lot with other airlines but this is our first experience with Virgin Atlantic. While the service by crew was on par, the layout and space was awful. First, there is less storage room overhead than any international flight I have been on, let alone in business class. There is no room for any personal item such as laptop bag storage - even in coach there is underwear storage space. The lay flat beds fold over which feels like a waste of space and requires passengers to get up and adjust. All the seats face each other across the aisle, which is weird for privacy. In short, stop trying to cram so many seats into business class. Charge more if you need to but make it decent. Not flying Virgin business class again and will actively tell others not to unless things have changed.

We were in seats 33A and 33C - would highly recommend these seats as they are the last seats in premium economy section with a bulkhead behind which allows you to have the seat reclined whenever you like without interfering with passengers behind you. The first row seats in premium economy s 31 similarly have no seating in front as on exit row but TV screens are either mounted in between the seats in a centre console or on the bulkhead in front, excellent legroom but screen position could be an issue.

Recently flew BA’s nonstop between Boston and London on the A380. It is a massive airplane with a payload of over 500 passengers. Business class seating on this plane and on this route was not worth the $$ in my opinion. There were too many seats in each row making the seats narrower than those offered by other airlines. Most jumbo jets have a 1-2-1 configuration in business class; this plane had 2-3-2 and 2-4-2, twice as many seats in each row. This is particularly obnoxious if you are seated in the middle aisle because that means anyone seated in a window seat or in the middle seats has to crawl over an aisle passenger just to get to the bathroom and back. If you do so in the dark on an overnight flight, it is actually unsafe for you and that poor aisle passenger. Check the plane scheduled for the flight you want to take and if a 777 is offered, opt for that one. They are all equipped with Club Suites in Business now.

A burlap sack full of field rocks would be a better seating experience. I have tried both the regular and plus seats in economy and both are absolutely abysmal, both for comfort and space. A true sardines in a crushed tin can experience.

Was sat on that famous row 35, seat 35H. Summary: 11.5 hours flight from LHR to GIG in seat that doesn't recline by default. The seats on the row 34 ahead recline, meaning it's a struggle for eating or drinking if passengers sat on row 34 keep their seats reclined. To make the disaster worse, the overhead bin compartment above rows 33 to 35 are occupied by cabin crew stuff. Means that it is extremely difficult to accommodate cabin luggage.

LATAM's seating policy is one of the worst I’ve experienced. Unless you're willing to pay extra, you're stuck with the most uncomfortable middle seats. Seat selection isn’t included, and their system is designed to push you into paying more for basic comfort. The seats are cramped, with minimal legroom, and the recline is barely noticeable. For such long flights, this is unacceptable. On top of that, the staff showed no flexibility in helping passengers who requested better seating due to special circumstances. If you're looking for comfort, either prepare to pay a significant amount on top of your ticket or avoid LATAM altogether. Their seating arrangements are a money grab, and customer care doesn’t seem to care.

The seat is 54 cm wide, but once converted into a bed, it expands to 62 cm, offering enough space to lie flat and sleep without feeling restricted. The bedding provided — including a mattress topper, duvet, and pillow — was high quality and made the bed genuinely comfortable. The layout feels private, thanks to the suite-style design. While the sliding partition isn’t full height, it gives a good sense of separation. There’s a generous amount of room around you, and the design is stylish but understated. There’s a large 32-inch screen right in front of the seat. The screen resolution was sharp, and the sound system came with noise-cancelling headphones. Storage space was enough for personal items. The table is large and stable. The seat controls were simple to use, and it was easy to find the perfect position for sitting, lounging, or sleeping. Cabin crew were attentive and respectful, always nearby without being intrusive.

Like the majority of their regular business class passengers I hate the business class seats on their A380 aircraft. The seat and surrounding environment are great for take-off, landing or whenever in the normal seated position. But when it comes time to sleep, then good luck with that one. It soon becomes the most uncomfortable business class lay flat bed in the sky. What were they thinking? Well clearly, they were not.  At least they are more likely to get a decent night’s sleep that the poor passengers trying to get comfortable on this seat. Please Singapore Airlines – do something to address this issue. Given these aircraft are most likely going to be around for a lot longer that initially planned, don’t make your loyal customers continue to suffer. At least get some decent bedding.

A major fatal flaw in the terribly designed business class seat which is truly awful if you want to try to sleep! While it’s a flat bed you are forced to sleep diagonally with very narrow footwells so that if you want to change position to lie on your side then your other side it’s impossible! It’s to restrictive to move so you’ll hardly get any decent sleep unless you have consumed large amounts of alcohol from the great choice on the wine list - whoever designed this seat needs to be fired! Apparently talking to one flight attendant they did say there’s a refit of new seats & interior on this aircraft planned but wasn’t sure when. Seat adjustment controls worked if you hold & press, which is a bit outdated & needs improvement. lighting was sufficient for reading. Privacy on an aisle seat is never any good so if that’s what you want then window seat is recommended. So A380-800 business class seat not recommended & if you want a good nights sleep & opt for the A350 or 777 aircraft with Singapore.
A320Neo with comfortable seat and good leg room and recline with adjustable headrest, USB port and outlet power.

Singapore Airlines have been updating their long-standing light-brown coloured economy seats with newer blue coloured seats. Whilst the inflight entertainment tech has certainly benefited, SQ have made a shocking choice of seat type / pitch. SQ state that these seats have a 32 inch pitch. I am definitely taller than average 6'8", but did fit in their previous economy seats. This is no longer the case. Whether it's due to the cushion thickness, design method of seat recline etc, the simple fact is that SQ's newer economy seats are far more cramped and uncomfortable. The SQ service remains good, but this doesn't really matter when you simply can't fit into their seats and experience genuine discomfort on long-haul flights. I experienced this issue on both their A350-900 and A380. In my opinion, when travelling long-haul, being in a seat with legroom and being comfortable, are the most important factors in choosing which airline to use next.

One of the most comfortable Boeing 777-300 with 3-3-3 seat layout in Y class. Great leg room and seat wide 45 cm,with seat power supply and big IFE screen. Unfortunately IFE was average mostly arabic and bollywood films

We flew from Vancouver to Paris and did not get anything extra other than a bag containing a toothbrush and a few other things compared to economy. We had one meal service and one snack before landing and they did not came around once in between the meal service. Terrible for premium economy.

QF7 - Sydney to Dallas - seats 37a & 37b - bulkhead behind seat. First time on Qantas premium economy, selected these seats as no interruption to recline with bulkhead behind. Very nice seats and good sized entertainment screen. Power options available. Great additional storage along window side, very handy. Didn't seem to be any issue for recline from the other premium seats. Very happy with seating choice - recommend.

The business class of British Airways flying London to LA is very poor by comparison to other airlines, for the price. The seating is narrow, on top of a neighbor, no separate little cabin. It's also generally more expensive and the Avios are not worth collecting as there is rarely any availability.
Worst seat in a Qantas International Business class product. 2x2 arrangement, old seat rather than one of the new seats. This seat hasnt changed in who knows how long.

I chose one of the best seats on this older configuration of 787. It was a window forward facing seat. They offer mattress, duvet and pillow. The seat length was very long but slightly narrow. The only storage was big enough for most stuff.

I paid for an economy plus seat and what I got was the exact same uncomfortable seat for all of economy and maybe 2 inches more leg room. This is a scam by the airlines to make money and sell a product that is not worth the money.

During this pandemic - I actually travelled Virgin Atlantic on the first trip after lockdown here in the UK that they had with passengers. Hiccups on the way were expected. The seat was wonderful, the leather is really soft and the crew are just brilliant. I had a bulkhead seat on 21A and there was plenty of legroom. Cabin Crew bring through these items that you can put your foot on, like a leg rest but it is moveable due to the bulkhead. My only downside would be that the screen is on the side of you and can get stuck when you try to stow it back to its original position.

The first class seat 4A is OK. The seat recline comfort and armresting is average. It's spacious enough, and fairly comfortable. However, the leg for say someone taller might be an issue with knee room restrictions. I'm 5'10. Especially, if the person forward of you reclines all of the way without any considerations. Bear in mind though that the row behind you is an economy one. There is NO physical bulkhead separation on these aircraft. Sometimes you'll get someone with happy feet kicking your seat. I hate this inconsiderate behavior. Knowingly or not. The direct overhead space (left aircraft seats with "A" designation. i.e. 1A, 2A, 3A, etc...) is for very small items. Like a coat or jacket. The overhead space in say seat 4B, you can fit a pretty good sized regulation carry on like a 22x14x8" or a good size back pack NO problems. All in all, the EMB 170/175/190's is a much more comfortable aircraft than say the older, very cramped ERJ135/145 regional jets.
Nice and comfy business class seat. The cabin staff were very attentive. I was offered business seat upgrade during my check in, which was a pleasant surprise, since my flight duration was 13hrs.
Seat has a good legroom. The screen size was excellent and the provision of power supply is also commendable.

It was an older Airbus A320 aircraft, but there were no issues and the hygiene was good. There wasn't a lot of space for my legs (186cm), but ok. But I need to say I had more space at an A320 aircraft from Vueling than with Brussels Airlines. The crew speaks fluently Dutch, French and English and will try help you if you have a question.

JFK to Boston last night. I was in seat 4A and paid extra for that seat. The seat in front of me did not go into the upright position and was declared broken by the flight attendants. My tray table was also broken and would not hold a drink. It was hanging from the back of 3A. The staff did not seem concerned that upon landing and takeoff, Seat 3A was in my lap and not appropriate. This does not even sound like acceptable safety standards, much less worth the price I paid for a ticket. The plane and the seat was also filthy and there was debris/food/grunge around the screen in front of me. The seat I was in was dirty with I arrived and basically I expect at least cleanliness from the plane during COVID. I wanted a refund in compensation for the less than acceptable trip. I received 25$ CREDIT. I would avoid this airline at all costs. You get what you pay for. Cheap flights. Unfortunately, they are the only choice sometimes. I have many more issues with Jet Blue and really hope that in their race to grab a portion of international travel, their standards are quite higher. The web sight and receipts have minimal information and I had to request it. I could not access my flight into if I was not on line, which is most of the time when I travel. Their app is AWEFUL. I could not get a hold of anyone to talk to. Used a chat session that was mostly script. I have flown small planes in 3rd world countries that have better standards that Jet Blu. The flight attendant was also surly and unresponsive to my concerns. They get a 2 only because it was the end of a 28hr day of travel and they got me where I wanted to be on time.

My initial booking was on Economy class and then I upgraded to business class after paying fare difference. Business class seat was uncomfortable. If you're seating on window seat and wanted to move from your seat you will not be able to leave your seat unless you disturb passenger that sitting next to your seat. And if passenger next to you is laying down and sleeping then you need to jump to pass or you must wake up him/she to move seat to seating position. Furthermore, service on board was not to level to business class as I was expecting. In addition, was surprised upgraded ticket was not included using airline lounge in Dubai Airport. Finally it is not worth paying so much money for upgrade to Business class on B787 300 aircraft.

The seats did not recline in any way and if you're a larger than a teenager you have absolutely no room to move in those seats there is no in-flight entertainment no comfortability if you suffer from restless leg syndrome do not fly with them you have no room to adjust your legs your knees are basically touching the seat in front of you.

This review refers to the Q suite, it really one of the very best in flying and luxury experience. It is almost like flying first class for the price of business. Try it for yourself if you can, you will see what I mean.

I booked seats 10J & 10K which are the front row in Economy Premium as I am 1.95m tall and I need the extra legroom. A few days before the flight I received a notice on my booking saying 'Due to operational reasons your seat has been moved to row 12". No other explanation and when I asked at the airport they could also not explain why the seat was changed. 12K is an appalling seat when you are tall and is not what one expects in premium economy at all. The seat was extremely narrow, cramped with minimal legroom. The two seats that I had booked were than randomly given to two young men (probably friends or relatives of KLM staff). The passenger in front of me kept his seat in full recline position and I could hardly move. He refused to put his seat up when I asked. The food was inedible with dry, thick sandwiches and unappetizing food. All min all this was an appalling experience and now I know why I changed from KLM to BA years ago - they change your seats at random for friends. I thought I would try it one more time but never again. I will be cancelling my return flight with a refund. The cost of the return flight for 2, with lounge access was NOK 31000 (US$4000). An outrageous price for nothing. Be warned

The seat width is acceptable but has limited storage space. It turns into a flat bed but it won’t recline the way airline seats do. Virgin supplies a mattress and a blankets, as well as a pillow for each seat. Operating the seat is reasonably user friendly and has ample privacy but this is not an enclosed suite. USB and electric outlets are provided. The screen size was large but you can’t watch it if stowed. They wanted you to stow the screen during take-off and landing but you can’t watch those safety videos from that angle. I am surprised how this design was approved. The entertainment videos are plenty to keep you busy in the sky and you can have WiFi as well although you have to pay extra. Overall experience was good.

Had the pleasure of experiencing the Business Studio product on the 787-10, and while it is  7 years old, it still is among my favorites. It offers a 180 degrees full flat bed and a handy control on the side of the seat and on the Inflight Entertainment screen. The seat comes with a bunch of adjustable features, such as seat cushion and a massage feature. I found the seat to offer a great amount of privacy. Also managed to get some work done while flying, the table is big enough and doesn't move too much. Very satisfied with this seat, would book again!
Q Suite (seat 1A) The best seat type in Business class, in terms of comfort and sleeping in. The flight attendants prepare your bed with a bed mattress, extra pillow and you get pajamas.

Aircraft was Thai's new B77-300ER. Seat layout is 3x3x3 and seem to be wider than other aircraft with 3x4x3 layout. Seat width seems OK because my shoulders were not bumping on to the person next to me (I was on an aisle seat). Seat pitch is fine at the start (I am 5'2") until the passenger in front of you recline their seat -- then your seat becomes uncomfortable and it becomes difficult to move your legs. Aisle space seems to be the same as other aircraft. Because there were fewer economy seats, thus fewer economy passengers, than in a 3x4x3 aircraft, we did not have to queue most of the time to use the toilets.

This was my tenth time flying on EVA air royal laurel class between Taiwan and US. The seat was really comfortable and provided a decent space for me to rest. The meal was fantastic too. And the cabin crews were friendly and provided excellent service which made it a very comfortable journey.

Cramped into an A330-300 economy seat. Knees were pressed hard into the seat row in front of me. Seat row pair in front of me was installed crooked (as in improperly). When the passengers in front of us reclined fully, the IFE screen was 6” from my face and the headphone jacks didn’t work. Armrests didn’t go up, so in an emergency, I could have been trapped as there was no room to get out of the seat unless I woke up the passenger in front of me and made them put their seat up. Hands down the worst trans-Atlantic crossing I’ve ever made. Avoid this airline.

I paid a premium to get leg room and all I got was a cattle class seat with my knees wedged into the back of the seat in front and a "free" meal in a cardboard box. One expensive meal that was! There was not even an empty seat in row 3, which is usually the case when using the front of the plane for premium. Just my wife, myself, and a stranger, crammed into three narrow seats. There were none of the other onboard courtesies normally afforded premium passengers, such a priority boarding or deplaning. The crew were pleasant enough, though nothing outstanding. There were WiFi connection cards in the seat pockets, but the plane was old and had no WiFi We did enjoy access to the lounge. Given CPH is one of SAS's home ports the lounge was far from resplendent. The food selection was minimal, nothing typically Scandinavian. Soup, salad, one beer, coffee, no deserts. I had to wait 10 minutes for a young man to stop fiddling in the kitchen and bring me a soup spoon.

In my opinion, I think Lufthansa is a great airline, but their economy class could use some work. When I last flown with them the food in economy was absolutely horrendous. it was a very messy meal and at the end my stomach was aching. Also the seats were very cramped, and there was not even enough legroom to stretch out even for me who is 5ft9. All and all Lufthansa is great airline but if they fixed these points, they would have a lot more customers.

The experience is better than many North American and European Airlines. The staff are still outstanding and professional. Nothing is too much trouble and the food is excellent. In flight services are all about the passenger and nothing is too much trouble. The seats are comfortable and for a 16 hour plus flight, this is essential. The only problem is that EVA Airlines keep the cabins very warm, to the point of hot. I woke literally soaked through with sweat which is exacerbated by the rules that masks must be worn unless eating. The warm temperature also seems counterintuitive when considering that this temp is ideal for illness but again, it is something that EVA can control. This is a small issue but it affects the comfort of the flight. Apart from that, the airline continues to maintain a strong focus on service.

Headrest is fixed and not changeable. Armrest are 2 small foldable tables.  IFE Flightinfo can not save changes to metric system by each change to movie or music an return to flight info. Touchbuttons to change the seat not working (crew needs to change the seat to bed). Bed is not to sleep for passengers who sleep on sides. Hole for feet is to small for footsize 46.

The fully lie-flat seats made for a good night’s rest, even if it was only for a couple of hours. I could stretch out fully at a height of 5’10” (180cm). Storage space and seat width and comfort is very much in line with the standard of international carriers but not exceeding expectations, hence their rating as a Skytrax 4-star Airline is just about right.

The design are beautiful with a great choice of colour. The seats are bit harder compare to the old seat but its slim design make leg room more spacious. The are no IFE but the are phone slot to replace IFE. For me, the seat comfort was moderate but suitable for my 2 hours journey flight.

I'm not expecting extreme seating comfort on a budget airline, but the quality of the seats in Flydubai is rather poor. Seats are lightly padded and flimsy, legroom is tight considering I'm just 5 feet 5 only. The seats can recline but minimal, which offers little to no extra comfort in addition to the uncomfortable seats already. I was surprised the is a touchscreen infotainment screen. The infotainment screen does offer an array of movies and trip information. I do not recommend flying with Flydubai. The seat comfort is mediocre and uncomfortable.

I was extremely disappointed when I messaged customer service that the Business class seat I upgraded to did not lay flat for the 11 hour trip. I emailed them saying that the cabin crew tried their best but they were limited to what they can do and they were great about it. I requested for just a refund of the upgrade and their response was to offer a payment of 50 EUR.

Worst business class seat I have experienced Automatic seat controls did not work on either the outbound or return flight, so flight attendant assistance was required several times. Same with the center wall divider partition that required attendant assistance to lock it in place for both flights. Seat design requires you to lie at an angle in order to use the foot rest space. Overall, was not impressed with this business class product &amp.

This seat is just not comfortable and my body was aching after a 2 hour flight from Munich to Catania. The only way to have a reasonably convenient flight in this seat is, when sitting in the first row. I reserved a first row seat and got a boarding pass for it but, when boarding was bumped backwards and had to squeeze into the limited space in the other rows in Business Class. Not a very nice feeling to be shown that it doesn’t really matter if one is loyal to Lufthansa. Like my last mid-distance flight on LHs A321 which even worse, I cannot recommend this aircraft for any flight other than very short haul, certainly not in business class and I definitely won’t pay the much higher price charged for this so called premium seat. But at least there was a USB charge point near the seat (in Evo and Business)

Terrible seat configuration, very old and inconvenient, lack of privacy. Seat uncomfortable, little controls for various seating and sleeping configurations. Lie flat seat malfunctioned and could not lie flat during the flight. Could not change to other business class seats as they were all occupied. The airline did not offer any partial refund, only future flight discounts of 15%. Terrible customer services. Will never fly on Turkish Airlines again. Many other better choices.

Worst business class seat I’ve ever had. Very thin cushioning, not comfortable. Bed cover is not a mattress at all, just a thin piece of material. You can’t lie straight, you have to lie on an angle and rest your legs on the footrest with your feet in a small cavity. Very poor for a business class product, Avoid at all costs.
For long haul flights the seats in economy are unacceptable, especially by paying extra for the 22A.

This review is for Warsaw to Chicago, Sept 5, 2023. Also, this is our first, and most likely last time we will fly on LOT. Positives: Very attentive and kind cabin crew. Plenty of beverages throughout the flight. Meals were somewhat basic (dinner and 'breakfast'), but adequate. Negatives: Very, very cramped. Not much space between rows, and even less when person in front of you reclines their seat. Given how little room there is, it is understandable that someone may want more space, but then there is no room to use your seat table. My wife had a drink on hers, which spilled when the person in front of her reclined their seat. If you drop something, good luck trying to find it while inflight. Aisles very narrow, barely any room to walk. For a 10+ hour flight, this is not a good choice.
9Boeing 777-300 is tatty and needs a refurbishment. The tray table is difficult to remove. On my seat in the premium exit row, the tv screen will not stay in place.

The seats are narrowest I have ever travelled on. I am a rather tall person (193cm) and I avoid low cost airlines because their seats are too narrow. If I knew that Iberia is operating as a low cost company, I would have preferred another airline.

This was an amazing seat. Better than delta! I flew from Seattle to Atlanta, and the seat was so wide. I was very impressed, especially for premium and economy. It also reclined with pretty decent reclining. However, there was no seat back entertainment. But that’s ok. I used my iPad. It was free. So yeah! Great experience. For good seats, I definitely recommend Alaska Airlines.

Seat was very hard and there was no recline. The legroom is fine if you're short, but if you are of average height (say 5'6" or more), you are going to struggle. No pouch to store anything, just a bare basic leather seat

The most uncomfortable seat encountered. Minimal padding, no lumbar support, extremely uncomfortable, for the 6 hour flight to Cairns from Singapore. Don't book, unless you want to be in extreme discomfort, and have back ache for a day or two after. I am 6 ft tall, slim and fit. I booked an exit row seat thinking it would be more comfortable, but the seat has a stub as an arm rest meaning it is about 13 inches wide in practice.
Cabin layout was great, cabin was beautiful and the seats were great good legroom and wider seats than usual in a 3-3-3 seat configuration also a lot more space

Uncomfortable seat for long-haul flight. Tasteless food. Hard working flight attendants who try to provide good service. Seat cushion is very thin over hard board underneath. Very uncomfortable lean-in to window. Leg room is sufficient. Audio-visual on seatback is totally unengaging. Music very limited, mediocre sound quality. While the flight attendants were quick to respond and courteous, a very uncomfortable seat that became nearly unbearable after 4 hours (16 hour flight) made the trip unacceptable quality. Terrible food , tiny quantities and no dessert. I would not recommend economy.

Regular business class passengers, we were (once again unfortunately) dealing with a maintenance problem with your equipment, namely your business seats. I had reserved seats 1D and 1E for my wife and myself and we had a very unpleasant surprise because upon boarding we were allocated other seats because the 1E was broken (and had been for several flights!). Initially the person at check-in separated us and at my insistence I was still able to have 2 seats side by side, and we were again moved for the second section towards Paris and this time right next to the WC where a painful flight! If I take the trouble to pay for business class and reserve seats 1D and 1E it is because we are very tall and the space for the feet is more important on these seats while all the others have a ridiculous little triangle for foot rest and it is almost impossible for us to sleep. In short, this is not the first time that I have experienced this type of problem with ATN and it is becoming really problematic. The business seats are in a deplorable state since some are patched up with plaster, others are dislocated (I took many photos of the cabin if you are interested). I had an interview with the purser who sent a message via her on-board iPad but it had no effect. Passagers régulier de la classe poerava business nous avons eu (encore une fois hélas) affaire à un problème d'entretien de votre matériel, à savoir vos sièges business. J'avais réservé pour mon épouse et moi même les fauteuils 1D et 1E et nous avons eu une très mauvaise surprise car dès l'embarquement on nous attribue d'autres sièges car le 1E était cassé (et ce depuis plusieurs vols!). Au départ la personne au check in nous séparait et devant mon insistance j'ai quand même pu avoir 2 sièges cote à cote, et nous avons encore était déplacés pour le second tronçon vers Paris et cette fois juste à coté des WC d'où un vol pénible !. Si je prend la peine de payer une classe business et de réserver les sièges 1D et 1E c'est que nous sommes très grands et l'espace pour les pieds est plus important sus ces sièges tandis que tous les autres ont un petit triangle ridicule pour repose pieds et il nous est quasiment impossible de dormir. Bref, ce n'est pas la première fois que je subis ce genre de problemes avec ATN et cela devient vraiment problématique. Les sièges business sont dans un état lamentables puisque certains sont rafistolés avec du sparadrap, d'autres sont déboités (j'ai fait de nombreuses photos de la cabine si cela vous intéresse). J'ai eu un entretien avec la chef de cabine qui a envoyé un message via son ipad de bord mais cela n'a eu aucun effet.

The seat was okay, it was kind of dirty in the side cracks! and my tv remote was stuck. They provided water in the cup holder of the seat which was nice. The seat was pretty soft, so it is good for sleeping.

Absolutely disgusting flight with TAP Portugal business class from Warsaw to Lisbon. They put a charter plane rented from Get Jet which is a low cost airline experience. The seat even in the front row (business class) is extremely cramped with no legroom whatsoever. Seats are very uncomfortable and just not worthy of any business class fare.

Having recently flown with Aegean Airlines, I found the legroom to be highly disappointing. As depicted in the attached image, the legroom is virtually non-existent. My knees were pressed against the seat in front of me, which made for an incredibly uncomfortable flight experience. When the passenger in front of me reclined their seat, it became impossible to move. This lack of space is a significant inconvenience. There is no improvement in space or comfort as you move towards the back of the plane, making it a consistent problem for a large portion of the cabin.  I would recommend Aegean Airlines to reconsider their seating configuration to enhance passenger comfort.

Sat in seats 24a outbound to Budapest and 18A return flight from Bucharest. Seats were both very worn and had a ridge running a couple of inches from the rear. My backside was numb on both flights and less than 3 hours for each flight. Legroom far to little for a national carrier. Also on the return flight the seat pocket had a hole at the bottom and only found this out when i put items in it and they fell on the floor and due to the lack of space had to ask fellow passengers if they could reach my stuff which they kindly did. USB charger  going very intermittent as well. I will avoid British Airways on short haul flights if possible.

While the staff, food and general communication with the airline through email and the app was really good both ways on my business class flights, the seats are like articulated coffins when you lie them flat. The planes seem to be older, I believe they are ex Philippine Airways. There is no mattress pad given to soften the sections in the seat as it moves to flatten out, so you are trying to lie on what feel like sideways slats - you can feel every single one! The area for your feet when the seat is flat is about a foot high and about 15 inches wide, so unless you only lie on your back there is no way to turn onto your sides. I fiddled around with the controls to see if I could get comfy for quite a while till I gave up, sat up, and leaned my head to sleep onto the shelf provided in the seat pod. It’s a terrible design and I had neck and back discomfort for two days post flight. Seats 7A and 7K. I was so disappointed as I had been looking forward to my flights for months. The good thing is that there is no one next to you and all the uneven numbered seats are right at the windows. Need to do better Lufthansa as otherwise I have no complaints.

This is a specific review of 68K I flew 68K on both legs LGW-DXB and DXB-SIN. This is an outstanding seat for legroom. If legroom is your priority, even with your own access to the seat, this is THE seat to go for in economy along with its corresponding seat on the port side. The legroom is basically full stretch and you can access in and out viw the gap in front with so much room that you won’t annoy the two seats to your diagonal front. There’s no danger of the people in your row using your corridor, especially if you extend the video monitor. The downside of this seat is of course no at seat storage for take off and landing, and the video monitor is a bit rubbish as is the flimsy tray extension. Neither USB port worked on my flights either. But it’s all about legroom and this excels.

Was sat on that famous row 35, seat 35H. Summary: 11.5 hours flight from LHR to GIG in seat that doesn't recline by default. The seats on the row 34 ahead recline, meaning it's a struggle for eating or drinking if passengers sat on row 34 keep their seats reclined. To make the disaster worse, the overhead bin compartment above rows 33 to 35 are occupied by cabin crew stuff. Means that it is extremely difficult to accommodate cabin luggage.

I consider American Airlines a world-class carrier with aspirations for excellence, so when I sat down at my seat and found the touch screen was not working. I thought, “Ok, it’s fine; this sometimes happens. This is okay.” Then I put my arm on the armrest and was surprised to see that the entire armrest was covered in duct tape, and I thought to myself, “Duct tape? really?!” If I rent a car, and upon getting in, find the seat is covered with duct tape, I would consider this unacceptable. So, for American Airlines, which has aspirations for excellence. My question is this: Is this acceptable?

The Embraer 175 is, without a doubt, a game-changer for regional travel. The first-class seat, designed for flights of up to 4.5 hours, offers unmatched comfort on shorter routes like the quick 27-minute hop from DCA to PHL. With ample legroom, supportive cushioning, and a well-thought-out design, there’s nothing to complain about, especially on flights averaging under an hour. It’s always surprising when infrequent travelers nitpick a product that delivers exactly what it promises. Republic Airways continues to provide a consistently solid experience for the American Airlines Group, reinforcing why the E175 remains the gold standard for regional flying.

Like the majority of their regular business class passengers I hate the business class seats on their A380 aircraft. The seat and surrounding environment are great for take-off, landing or whenever in the normal seated position. But when it comes time to sleep, then good luck with that one. It soon becomes the most uncomfortable business class lay flat bed in the sky. What were they thinking? Well clearly, they were not.  At least they are more likely to get a decent night’s sleep that the poor passengers trying to get comfortable on this seat. Please Singapore Airlines – do something to address this issue. Given these aircraft are most likely going to be around for a lot longer that initially planned, don’t make your loyal customers continue to suffer. At least get some decent bedding.

Non existing leg room at all I am 6.2inches tall it was plain and simple torture you think that if you paid premium seats you will have leg room not at all plus you have to pay for everything. I will not fly ever again in this Airline. Also the seat won’t recline at all. Horrible, this is ok only for kids and people less than 5 ft tall.

I was shocked to see how close the rows were placed. I am an average height woman and have never had a flight where my knees almost touched the back of the seat in front. Getting in and out was very difficult, particularly if the person in front was reclining. In fact, when they reclined, it was best to also recline. I had a 12+ hour flight, followed by a 6+ hour flight, too long to be so cramped. The seats were more narrow that usual and the aisles also narrow, I wasn’t sure until my return journey with another airline.Their seats are definitely wider, as are the aisles and there was much more room between the row seats. It was so obvious that when my son & I boarded, I remember saying to him 'this feels like business class after the trip over.' He was shocked as he flew the other airline both ways. Sadly for this reason, I would never fly with Etihad again.

We booked Business Class to enjoy a pleasant flight with extended periods of sleep during the flight. We had seats 11D and 11 G, seats that did not have any privacy screen around the seats like the other seats in the Business Class cabin. We got the impression that these seats were added on to maximise the seating in Business Class without any consideration to the comfort of passengers, who paid substantial fees to have the benefits of a Business Class. The seats were adjacent to the two toilets at the front of the cabin, with regular traffic to and from there, with people waiting in the aisle to use the toilets. All the other passengers in the cabin were enclosed and protected by the privacy screens. In addition, the cabin crew made lot of noise in the kitchen area, dropping on numerous occasions metal kitchenware, chatting loudly after lights-out, not respecting our need for a rest. The service was very hectic, we got the impression that the crew had not been trained sufficiently. As far as food was concerned, a number of the items on the cabin menus were not available, or prepared in the kitchen area, as we could witness since most of the time the curtains were not closed. Also, all meals had to be served on hand-held trays carried by the crew through the cabin. This caused extensive delays in serving meals. After several hours of coping with the below-standard seat and service situation, I requested alternative seats from the head stewardess, which she could not provide due to the fact that some business-class seats were already occupied by staff members returning home. So, we were put up in two Premium Economy seats, which provided no opportunity to get any sleep.
Economy layout with 2-4-2 but nice seat with great legroom (83 cm) and 45 cm seat wide. Seats are equipped with with big IFE sceen and power supply as well as the holder for own smartphone or tablet
Flight on Airbus 320. The cabin was a little worn off but clean, seat itself was okay. Not very comfortable but okay for a short flight. Bathroom was clean.

We recently travelled Auckland - Singapore -London - Singapore - Auckland, on both the A350 and B777. Service was perfect, as usual, and food quality was generally good.Entertainment seems to have declined. The great disappointment was the Business Class seat, same on both aircraft. It cannot be fully reclined without conversion to a bed, and to put your feet up requires twisting diagonally into a barely comfortable position. Not much better when fully flat in bed form. I have travelled on Singapore business and first over almost 30 years, and this seat is the worst i have experienced.

I flew ITA Airways on flight AZ857 (14 Oct 2025) and was assigned seat 33F, an emergency-exit row seat. Only after take-off did I discover that the seat did not recline at all. This was not indicated during booking, check-in, or boarding. On a 6.5-hour overnight flight, being unable to recline made it impossible to rest and resulted in a very uncomfortable journey. Exit-row seats are usually sold as extra legroom, so ITA should disclose when a seat cannot recline so passengers can make an informed choice.

I paid 90 AED for seat 1A, but the seat was stuck in a reclined position for the entire flight. I reported it to the flight attendant, but she said they couldn’t fix it. Although the crew was polite, it was disappointing to pay extra for a seat that wasn’t fully functional.

Seats on the aircraft were old and outdated, and had seen better days. Inflight entertainment system reflected this with slow responsiveness. Seats offered little lumbar support, leaving the traveler after a long haul flight needing a soft surface to recover. The seats were extra legroom, bulkhead seats with no under seat storage.

AC633 on 6 January 2026, our assigned seats were 19H and 19J, originally intended for my 13‑year‑old daughter and 6‑year‑old son. Shortly after takeoff, water began leaking onto these seats. I reported the issue to the flight attendants, who told me it was “normal due to condensation.” Despite this explanation, the leak continued throughout the flight, with water dripping onto us and soaking our clothes. This made the journey extremely uncomfortable, especially for children. The only assistance offered was a napkin, which was clearly inadequate for an ongoing leak. No one followed up, offered alternative seating, or showed concern for the discomfort and wellbeing of my children or myself. For a long‑haul international flight, this level of service and care is unacceptable.

My family and me were on our way back from 11 day holiday in Turkey, where we've been given 10a-c and 11a-b seats on boarding. Later we learnt those are emergency seats. When airplane started taxiing, crew chief came to my 16 yrs son seating on 10a and told he must leave that place because airline rules. He was separated from the rest of the family to the rear seats. Flight attendant told I can join him after the takeoff, but other attendant didn't allow that. I sent the complaint feedback asking why my son was separated from us, while my 15yrs daughter kept sitting on 11a - emergency exit. I asked why they issued us those boarding passes if that's against security rules? Did the airlines expose my daughter's and other passengers' lives to danger, because they didn't move her to other seat? I tried twice to get the answer, but they're obviously not reading the feedback carefully. They answered only to the reason why my son is displaced, not the other questions. It's very disappointing and will try to avoid THY as much as I can, since they not trying even to give serious explanation or apology.
My seat is 25D, near the walk-way, the footrest is narrow, no screen in front of the seat and it is upholstered with leather and I don't like it. It's just okay.

The service was extremely good and I like to personally name the crew on board who performed this service on flight QR 274 on the 16th of April 2021 from Amsterdam to Doha, thank you very much: Faishal, Rudy, Prudence and Lynda, it was a joy flying with you.

This was a Boeing 777-300ER on one of Emirates' older aircraft that did not have  lie-flat seats.  The drawback I would find on this flight was the 2x3x2 configuration (no direct aisle access for window seats and the one middle seat) and how uncomfortable the seat is especially while sleeping.

I was pleasantly surprised with a lie flat business class seat for a less than 2 hour flight from Delhi to Mumbai. The seat was very comfortable with lot of storage, generous recline and ample leg room. It is slightly angled away to offer additional privacy. The IFE screen was quite large and easy to control with a touch screen controller. Charging slots are a bit only placed when you are seated but easily accessible when the seat is in lie-flat or recline mode. I used the lie-flat mode after breakfast and found it quite comfortable for a 6 foot adult passenger and could take a restful nap. Unsure about how comfortable this would be for long-haul but for medium-haul business this is a very comfortable seat.

JetBlue two weeks after I booked my tickets sent me an email that they moved my assigned seats as they claimed aircraft was changed. When I checked they took me out of my premium seats which I paid $147.00 and not only did not reimburse me but tried to charge me again when I tried to move my seats back. When I called the airline the JetBlue employee was not able to adjust the seats and had no idea what happened. I had to waste over 45 minutes on the phone after they called me back and still did not get the issue fully resolved. I booked 6 seats of which 2 were premium and they had no explanation as to why they moved all of our seats and why they moved everyone away from their travel companion.

The seat on the TUI Boeing 787-9 is very good after using 4 times long and short haul, I flew 9:30 to Jamaica in 2019 and the seat did get a bit cramped but that’s expected really after that time. The TV is acceptable but is not the biggest but does the job with an acceptable amount of content. The recline was pretty average. Overall the TUI Economy 787 seat was just above average quality and works great

The seat was unusually thin, the coating of it felt like fabricated plastic. The seat did not recline nor did it have a moveable head rest. Fortunately, the leg room was pretty decent. There was enough room to put my backpack under the seat. The seat is comfortable for the first 2 or 3 hours of the flight, however after that it becomes very uncomfortable. Good enough for a budget airline though!

Virgin Atlantic service was exceptional but the seats layout was awkward. There was simply no privacy but I would admit the seat was very comfortable. This particular B787 seats are complicated to operate and simply not practical. USB power was not working. Food service was good although with a limited menu. Flight attendants were always there with professional service. The H lounge at LHR is also one of the best.

I have chosen to give this airline an 8/10 review because the product was exceptional and the soft product, whilst still very good, is a bit underwhelming.  I boarded the plane and was warmly welcomed by the crew as they pointed to my seat, 2D. They promptly served a variety of pre-departure beverages from which I choose the fresh orange juice. Quality Arabic coffee was also served at this time. hot and cold towels were also distributed and the crew came round to ask for our meal choices. Once the plane had finished refueling, we began to take off for Bahrain. Soon after reaching the cruising altitude, I began to watch a movie and starters were served. Unfortunately, the cabin crew gave me the wrong starter. Upon bringing it up to them, they gave a rather sincere apology and gave me the correct starter of a simple yet tasty mozzarella salad. After that, mains were served and I got a rich chicken à la king with apple juice to drink. There was a noticeable gap in service between mains and desserts but I eventually got my dessert of a chocolate cake with tea. Soon after, I went to sleep after reminding the crew to wake me up for breakfast. I might have slept too deeply because the crew couldn't wake me up but fortunately, they still had breakfast available but it was not something to write home about. There was a selection of dry pastries which were worse than my economy meal. Soon after that we landed in Bahrain Airport. Overall I would say that the seat was exceptional but the food could be better in some way. Also, the crew did an exceptional job and I can understand why they left me to sleep.

This was my second trip on Frontier from Philadelphia to Cancun and back. The trips were 17 days apart. On both trips I upgraded to “stretch seat”, it is worth it, there is one particular seat above the wing (photo attached) that does not have a seat in front that is the best seat if you don’t mind being on the wing right next to an engine. From Philadelphia to Cancun was about four hours and three hours coming back. These seats held up well for that time and I was as comfortable as I could be for the product offered. An additional benefit of the stretch seats is that you can also recline. The tray tables are super small but you really don’t need them for much, so their size did not matter to me. Frontier is an ultra low cost airline so you pretty much get what you pay for, if you can spare the extra money, go for the stretch seating on flights that are three hours or longer.

The Big Seat!  I was flying to New Orleans for a conference and splurged for the Big Seat. It was the longest flight I had ever taken with Spirit. Everyone I think knows you can only last a few hours in a regular economy seat. Well, at first when I sat down in the Big Seat, the bottom half of the seat sagged and left an uncomfortable gap between the bottom and back rest. I just overlooked that and just hoped for the best. After all the seats do have a leather pillow added to the head rest for extra comfort, wrong! About 20 minutes of leaning my head on this, I started to feel some pain in my neck. It was really hard to get comfortable after this point and the pain in the back of my neck turned into a cramp like feeling. The only way I could get comfortable was to slide my head off the sewn in pillow so my head was more inline with the rest of my body. Turns out the pillow was extending my head forward so much that it was causing neck cramps. So my experience with paying extra for this supposedly upgraded seat turned out to be a total dud. It may be ok for some people but the comforts of upgrading to the Big Seat is not for me or everyone. Will be sticking to exit row seats and shorter flights under 3 for this airline.

Other than the fact that there is almost no leg room and seat recline is minimum, my biggest complaint is the seat itself. Specifically, the seat cushion, which was beyond uncomfortable. The seat cushion had been compressed /crushed to a point where you either have to sit in a slouched position or you have to sit on a bump near the back of the cushion. This is not the first time I have encountered this problem on a Sunwing plane. Come on Sunwing, either invest in better seats, or change the cushions regularly.

Let me preface this review by saying that I'm 6'3, so I'm generally challenged for space in Economy, but despite the fact that 23C is an isle seat, this was definitely and positively the worst seat I've ever had the displeasure of occupying on an airplane. Already when the seat in front of me was still upright I was struggling to focus my eyes on the screen, because it was that close. When the seat in front of me reclined fully, I was literally unable to remain seated. I spent my time sitting on a pillow across the armrest with the legs in the isle, getting up when folks needed to pass, which is obviously not safe and not allowed. A kind flight attendant took pity on me and found a seat more suited for my anatomy. I can't imagine how horrible this 11 hour flight would have turned out to be, had it been completely full.

I always have a good experience on Air France flights, especially now that US Airlines have overall dropped so much in quality, but there are small things that keep annoying me. In particular, I keep wondering why is it that they have head sets with two-prong jacks (with one that you have to fold on the side), when the actual jack plug has only one hole (see photo attached). Furthermore, the stereo sound often doesn't work and plays only in one ear (that was the case on my flight last Monday). Does that make any sense at all? On top of that, the USB port below the TV screen was not working, so I could not charge my phone. It's too bad, because I do like AF in general.
The seat was good and comfortable enough for 1 hour+ flight. The width is big enough for my body. The legroom is modest. Adjustable headrest well function. Lucky enough to occupy all three seats.

I had a very comfortable seat (17C) with extra room for my legs, as there is no seat in front. However, if you prefer having a possibility to stow small things in a seat or wall pocket during your flight, that seat might not be for you, as there is none. Also your screen is retractable, which means you can’t use it during takeoff or landing. However, with a tablet, you fine (besides not being able to stow it).

The seating is very cramped and uncomfortable with less legroom particularly for tall individuals. It feels like they are maximising revenues with addition of more seats thereby reducing customer comfort. Worse still the cabin crew is unhelpful and leaves customers fending for themselves. Cabin crew walking in the aisle keep brushing passengers sitting on the aisle seat. The headphone jack sound was not clear, there was loose connection. The display abruptly shut down for a few random seats some time down the flight and took long to restart again. Display was not responding. Cabin storage space was also relatively less. The crew was clueless on what caused the shutdown. The power plug too was slow to charge cellphone.

The most uncomfortable flight I have experienced due to the metal boxes under the seat in front. Outbound chose a window seat on lower deck and had one metal box under my seat that made sitting straight very difficult, so on way home opted for an upper deck seat in a set of two with my husband so I could at least get up and stretch. There was two boxes this time, and had pins and needles in my legs for not only the entire flight but for several hours afterwards. As vegan flyers we are never wowed with food, but this one was the worst yet, plain rice and vegetables.

Pleasant cabin layout. Good chair. But avoid row 34 since that's the row without one of these great 787 windows. No info at booking, so take care if you like a seat with a view. Seating quality is ok.

Bearable seats with storage space underneath the seats; however, the TV entertainment is awful. The screen is sluggish and not too touch sensitive. I've a hard time navigating the menu and movies/shows. Improvements needed.
Airbus 320neo. Horrible seat pitch my knees touched the front seat.  No comfort I had to sit sideways. The seats are semi hard and narrow width.

Seat 12F. This was a great seat for the price paid for my ticket (£24). I chose random allocation so I didn't pay for the seat. I was given 12E (the middle seat - a classic Ryanair punishment for not paying for a seat, but the 12F passenger didn't show up so I moved. I had a small under seat bag, and still had plenty of legroom.

This is a standard, small aircraft used for by KLM Cityhopper short city connections within mainland Europe. The plane was clean and there is enough room in the aisle to board and move around. There is not much storage space in the overhead compartments because this is such a small plane. The seat is wide enough for a normal-sized person and there is enough distance to the seat in front. There is more space than in similar planes of KLM’s low-cost subsidiary Transavia. A free piece of pastry and a drink was served.

This was a very nice experience. The steward was extremely friendly and attentive. The seat was roomy, comfortable and had it own sliding door for privacy. The food was delicious and service impeccable. As this was an overnight flight, whilst changing into the complementary pajamas, the flight attendant prepared my bed, with mattress and pillow case. Altogether, this was a perfect experience.

Low cost seats. The seats are so uncomfortable, no padding. I’ve had more comfort on a bus. It’s just Ryanair in red. For the price paid for the flight you’d expect more. The prices are no longer cheap.
Flight was over 6 hours, seats did not recline and I have never been more uncomfortable in my life. I have seen this for small commuter flights, not long ones like this. Just horrid

Chose a window seat so I could lean against the pillow and window as I usually do. But due to large gap between seat and arm ready window side it was very uncomfortable. Leg room minimal. I’m 5,5 . It seems new but not well designed. Tray table not adjustable and too close to body.

Took a flight at 25B on A320neo (SX-NEO) with Aegean's new cabin layout and in short it feels like a downgrade. I am an Aegean frequent flyer (Gold Miles&Bonus). The good: USB (B type) power for all passengers, place to put your phone/tablet in front of you, lighter/fresh cabin colors. The bad: New seat feels claustrophobic as the upper part of the front seat takes more area in front of you, the lower part of front seats seem bulkier now resulting to less legroom space, resulting obstructed access to aisle (you have to walk diagonally and you need to hold onto something). In addition to moving the toilets to the rear end to fit a new seat row, making them also claustrophobic, overall the new cabin is a downgrade.

Business Class cabin on the 777–300 (Non-ER, 777-31H) was very dated and disappointing. Stepping into the Business cabin fitted in a 2-3-2 layout, even the most seasoned of frequent fliers would be forgiven for mistaking the cabin for a premium economy cabin. Seats were not lie-flat and could only recline to a 120° angle, touchscreens were not only small at 13” but also very slow to respond and the entire hard product was no better than it’s own Premium Economy product on it’s newer A350s. It was the first time that I have not been able to get even a minute of shut-eye in a Business cabin. The cabin crew did well to make up for the abysmal hard product by providing exemplary service and meticulous attention to detail extending beyond just during the meal service. Their warmth partially made up for the disappointment and as a consolation, the flight arrived on time and check-in baggage did not go missing. One thing to note would be that most of the 777s in the Cathay fleet should already have undergone the retrofitting process to the updated 1-2-1 configuration using the Cirrus seat, which reclines into a fully flat bed and offers direct aisle access. The A350s come with the same configuration direct from the factory, bypassing the retrofitting process. These particular B777-non-ER 2-3-2 business class configuration which I am reviewing seem to be present predominantly on the shorter routes, used to regional destinations like Taipei, Seoul, Osaka and Tokyo.

Economy Seats are terrible, if person is reclined you can’t get out, the seats are not comfortable. Customer service English is not good. I cant make my flight because the connection is late,  so my new flight the next day will be at 2030 when they mean 1230 is a problem. I was told i would not be reimbursed since my flight the next day was early. Wont fly on this airline again.

The cramped leg space left many passengers uncomfortable, and despite the efforts of the flight crew, the situation remained unaddressed. The seats were not comfortable for long-distance travel, resulting in jammed knees and severe pain.
Wide and comfortable with enough legroom. Clean, perfect level of recline. Headphone and control point on the seat. Seat covers were good and clean, looked new and properly maintained.
