First and last flight with Hong Kong Airlines. Assured of good flying weather we had the seat belt sign on due to turbulence. Also a unpleasant, checkin on line, catch. Unless you pay for a seat at online check-in you cannot complete the check-in online and avail yourself of a bag drop. The airbus Hong Kong to Osaka was tired worn and not checked for seat maintenance. My seat 55J kept on reclining, I asked for an alternative and not offered one, no apology just continually told to return it to upright for take off.. The seat in front in lay back protruded as per photo. Clearly not only my seat was in a state of disrepair. Seat coverings were also showing signs of wear and lack of care and the seat cushion flattened not offering much support.
The middle seat is very squishy. I’d recommend choosing an aisle seat and as upfront as possible. It’s worth to pay for extra legroom in the exit door rows.

These are new seats and really comfortable. I had a window seat which faces slightly towards the window which was nice for the views and also it faces away from everyone else. The monitor is quite large and touch screen and has a remote by the side of the seat. The seat can turn flat when i am sleeping and was really comfortable. There was lots of storage which was great and sockets for power.

I had confirmed the seat suitable for my needs, had the seat confirmed with the boarding pass printed and issued to me. At the point of boarding I was told my seat was moved with no real reason given although we suspect it was to accommodate other passengers who do not seem to have any real reason to need to take over my seat. I ended up having to sit with the bad ear nearer to the aisle and could not hear what the flight attendant was saying. I am most displeased at this inconsiderate change without any prior discussion with me by the airline.

The Qsuite seat was terrific with lots of privacy and wonderful amenities. IFE, blanket, pillows and food were all excellent. Seat comfort for sitting or sleeping is great. Unparalleled service as well.

We paid $92 USD for extra legroom, which granted us barely more than the cheapest seats on Delta airlines. As long as you place backpacks and other under seat items in the overhead bins, you may have enough space to stretch your legs straight forward in front of you. The seats are nearly wide enough for a person wearing a US man's medium to fit, barely. They're hard, like folding wooden chairs, with little padding and forcing you to sit at an angle that pinches the sciatic nerve, even when reclined. When the person in front of you reclines, the TV is extremely close to your eyes and there's no room to get up at all. The aisles are so skinny, walking up and down them for relief is not an option, unless you walk sideways. The staff bump the carts along all of the seats up and down the aisles, so you have to sit with your arms crossed and shoulders pulled in, which causes pain in the back and neck.

The economy seats had barely any room between rows. If you were taller than 5'9" there was insufficient leg room. The entitled person in the seat in front decided to fully recline making a barely tolerable situation worse. When asked to limit the recline he responded that he needed to sleep. If seat room gets any closer, we'll be sharing seats or standing to fit more people on a plane. The tight connection from Vienna to Munich meant we had to jog to make our international flight, which is why our luggage is arriving tomorrow. Stewards were pleasant.

Flight on a 737, business/first class is 16 seats in 4 rows. Seats are generally comfortable, wide, with adequate legroom. Other than that there is nothing to differentiate them from a coach seat. No longer get a screen, no longer get any kind of priority wifi service, no longer offered headsets, no big screen, no options. Connectivity is mediocre mostly. This is a 4 hour flight. All the airlines are the same with some route exceptions.

The service was terrific but could not overcome the fact that the business class seat / bed did not function. The flight attendant had to lower it from sitting to fully reclined and back again, there was no in between setting. I was told that 11 of the about 120 seats were out of order. Do Not Fly this airline unless it is coach. Also, it was late taking off all three flights.

Flying American Eagle on Republic Airlines’ Embraer E175 is a game changer compared to other models. The spacious 2-2 seating in Economy means no middle seats, and First Class offers a private 1-2 layout perfect for solo travelers. The larger overhead bins fit standard carry-ons, so there’s less gate checking hassle. Plus, the bigger windows and ergonomic seats make for a more comfortable ride. Another major perk?… The E175 has two bathrooms, unlike some smaller regional aircraft that only have one in the back making the E175 more convenient for passengers. Given Republic’s excellent service and commitment to passenger comfort, American Airlines should seriously consider bringing them into their group of wholly owned carriers. Their operation stands out, and integrating them could further strengthen the American Eagle brand.

I have flown on Alaska Airlines for many years. My experience has been usually positive. Good Food, sometimes excellent. On my latest trip from MCO-PDX the food was excellent and service was attentive, and professional. I'm 6'3" and Alaska by far has the most legroom and recline of all, except Trans-con Business/First on Delta, American, United and Jetblue lie flat seats. Portland is a hub airport. I can usually travel to any significant U.S city non-stop and 1 stop to any European City.

Nice seat with a lots of leg room, you can stretch your legs without any problems, maybe a little narrow if in the middle Seat. Normal storage in seat pockets and usb entry. Screen good size but terrible sound.
New Boeing 777-300ER with 3-3-3 seating, wide seats with good leg room and recline with adjustable headrest. personal IFE, foldable table, tablet or mobile phone holder, USB port and outlet power.

Singapore Airlines have been updating their long-standing light-brown coloured economy seats with newer blue coloured seats. Whilst the inflight entertainment tech has certainly benefited, SQ have made a shocking choice of seat type / pitch. SQ state that these seats have a 32 inch pitch. I am definitely taller than average 6'8", but did fit in their previous economy seats. This is no longer the case. Whether it's due to the cushion thickness, design method of seat recline etc, the simple fact is that SQ's newer economy seats are far more cramped and uncomfortable. The SQ service remains good, but this doesn't really matter when you simply can't fit into their seats and experience genuine discomfort on long-haul flights. I experienced this issue on both their A350-900 and A380. In my opinion, when travelling long-haul, being in a seat with legroom and being comfortable, are the most important factors in choosing which airline to use next.

The seats had less recline than ANA - which we flew coming to San Francisco airport. United Airlines is not the worst, but I can hardly recommend it. If there was any other option to fly into las vegas, I would take that instead.

Philippine Airlines adds one more seat in the row in Economy class which gives a seat configuration of 3-3-3. A configuration found in aircraft with a wider cabin. A330 are usually configured 2 - 4 -2. In addition the seat distance is made for locals. I am 183cm and my knees touched the seat in front. There are charging ports for the phone but they did not work. There is no Inflight Entertainment Screen or connection for a headphone. On the seat is written that there is WIFI but it did not work.

Horrible seat. No storage space beneath seat or overhead because another passenger put their bag up there. Very small labels to identify which is the correct seat and the cabin crew don't bother to give directions. No legroom, power sockets or entertainment. Wobbly tray table. Armrest was sticky and seat had droplets on it. At least I wore dark clothing to hide it rubbing off.

The business class of British Airways flying London to LA is very poor by comparison to other airlines, for the price. The seating is narrow, on top of a neighbor, no separate little cabin. It's also generally more expensive and the Avios are not worth collecting as there is rarely any availability.

The smallest leg room I have seen. Customer reclined the seat in front of me is less than 30cm from my face making it impossible to watch a movie as the screen is too close.  Absolutely horrible experience.

BA used a configuration of 2x3x2 seats per row. I was seated in a middle, small, claustrophobic cabin in the middle with no air flow. Service was handled over a passenger seating on both sides and stepping to the aisle required jumping over another passenger.

I flew with Lufthansa with the new cabin, called Allegris. There is so much more legroom, compared to normal economy seats, the screen is 13.3 inches with a very high quality 4k screen. On the screen there is a USB-A port, a USB-C port and the port for the headphones that they and out. A very nice thing is that you can connect your bluetooth headphones to the entertainment screen. You can connect to the wi-fi for free if you have a miles and more account, but the free part is only for messaging.The seats were much more reclinable. The food was really good, compared to a lot of other airlines; we had the classic choice of chicken or pasta. I chose chicken and it had a curry sauce on the side and vegetales. After that I watched a movie on the intertainment screen, where there were a lot of choices. After I finished the movie, I slept for 6 hours on a 9 hour flight from Chicago to Munich. Around 40 minutes before landing they gave us a snack. The landing was really good! It was a butter landing! The cameras were really on the plane on the entertainment screen were a very interesting thing, especially because there were cameras for all of the angles, from the tale of the plane, to the under of the plane; it was also on both sides of the plane, showing the engine and part of the wing. Overall, the flight was very smooth and comfortable, showing that Lufthansa really thought this thru.

I am unhappy that despite speaking to a rep twice to ensure my family would be seated together, at check in we were separated. The worker at the gate could not have cared less. The airline does kit know anyone’s medical or immune status. Given Covid they should make lite if an effort to respect requests and if not, there is no need to be rude.

A fairly typical layout for business class on a Boeing 787. The seats are made of fabric and are comfortable. You can adjust the firmness of the seat and there is a massage feature (fairly basic though). One sandwich was provided on the 1.5-hour flight from Hyderabad to Delhi which is reasonable considering the duration of the flight and the fact this trip was during the COVID pandemic. The seat was comfortable and wide enough for me to expect a good sleep, a minor inconvenience would be having to step over your neighbour if you happen to have one. All in all, a nice flight

The seat was excellent. It's a bit old and the tray table shows its age, but given the fact it's old, it's the old-school type of leather seats. It's very wide and comfortable to take a nap. The seat and cabin in general was very clean and the crew sanitized my tray table when they served me my snack, so the seat was very clean. I would agree that TAR needs to refurbish their cabins but as of now, they're very good anyway.
Cramped seat in so-called Polaris class. No room for legs with seat fully extended. Worst business class seat ever. United should just rip out these seats and start over again.

Small legroom like most European airlines, but not that bad for tall people, this is because although the legroom is small, the seats don't recline, and for tall people, at least for me is a big plus, because once the seats in front of you recline, the legroom is completely gone. With Ryanair you are guaranteed that the person in front if you will not recline the seat, and since Ryanair trips are not long haul, I'd say its a good compromise for tall people.

Seating seemed to be the same as Economy, with the exception that the middle seat was kept empty, and there was more leg room. I found the legroom to be ample and I am fairly tall. Standard recline. Not particularly wide, but I am!  The price was reasonable.

The seat was very comfortable with enough legroom for someone as tall as me (6'3). I liked the width which was ok for a long-haul flight, the seat offers recline and has an Inflight Entertainment System, which features a ton of movies, tv-series, games, music, and much more. The seat even has a USB port so you can charge through the power outlet.

Seat was decent and clean, the legroom and seat width is sufficient. But one thing that annoys me is the seat recline not functioning. The economy class cabin needs refurbishment because it is still the same cabin I have been a few years ago. The seat does not have a headrest. The IFE system is decent but outdated although the entertainment content is still up to date. The interface needs a new look, including the system and console itself.

This is the second flight with Air Transat in the last 2 months. Although these planes are newer, the seat comfort is quite terrible. Anyone dealing with any back issues or lower back problems, please re-think this airline. My second flight confirmed why I should avoid Air Transat. It's not worth the cost of the pain, massages and possible chiropractor you will need to recover from these seats. I was on a 5 hour flight - and 4 days later I am still dealing with the pain of those seats.

The seats are 2x2x2 in individual suite configuration. The seat width was very comfortable. Seats were lay-flat made of plush textile and well maintained. The inflight entertainment system was great and had a large selection of movies and TV shows.

For this particular trip back home to Philadelphia from Las Vegas I upgraded to the Big Front Seat. The flight was a little bit over five hours and it was better from my original flight to Las Vegas on a regular seat. I find that the older models have a more comfortable Big Front Seat with more legroom. Although the new airplanes look and feel great, there is an overall issue with comfort and you still feel cramped in, even in row 1. I have made the decision not to fly Spirit on flights longer than 3 hours. Sadly their product is not designed for longer than that.

Unbelievably disappointed. So long as this seat design exists I will never travel with SAS again. I buy premium economy seats when I travel with family. I’ve flown on dozens of different airlines all over the world. I don’t buy business on family trips because of one very specific reason, the lift up hand rests. The ability to open up horizontal space and snuggle with my significant other is essential. These seats suck. They are as narrow as domestic economy, and they have massive thick metal barriers between each seat that cram you in. This is hands down the most uncomfortable seat I’ve flown on in years. What a joke.

The seat was a bit narrow albeit well padded. The legroom was a bit cramped maybe because I had a large backpack with me, the legroom would have been better otherwise. The seat didn't recline, the seat table was sturdy although it would be better if it was a bit bigger. The seat is perfectly good for a two hour flight and it is a quite comfortable seat.

Since covid I've tended to choose business class to ensure my wife and I can avoid sitting close to strangers and travel in our own bubble. That's why I chose Icelandair Saga class. We were booked on a B757 with a 2x2 configuration and checked in with seats 4D and 4F (window and aisle). But at the last moment the aircraft was switched to a B767 with 2x1x2 configuration. 4D became a orphaned middle seat with 4F across the aisle and an unknown stranger in the new window seat 4G. I wouldn't have known except for monitoring the inbound aircraft on Flight Radar 24. We protested at the gate and the agent told us no F and Gs were available, despite this flight's having been booked as a B757. Eventually she gave in and moved us, though only by shunting some other miserable passenger out of 4G that she hoped would make less fuss. Icelandair promote "free seat selection" as a reason for choosing Saga class, yet their unreliability as to which aircraft they're using turns it into a lottery. Apart from this bad start, we found the seats comfortable, but ours was a relatively short flight (KEF-LHR). Transatlantic passengers need to be aware of what they're getting: a wide reclining seat similar to short-haul domestic first class in the USA, but certainly no sleeper. The IFE is varied but the screens are annoyingly unresponsive. Very nice headphones, though.

The monitor in seat 68B would randomly shut off and the headphone jack was broken, this is very disappointing especially on a long flight; I had the same problem the last time I flew with them, why can't they fix their electronics? When returning on September 25th PR117 my selected seat was changed, I was told there was nothing they could do. I selected a window seat; why couldn't they accommodate me with a similar seat? They were extremely reluctant to help, they just kept saying that they reserve the right to switch the seats.

I paid extra in order to select a seat for my wife and myself toward the front of the plane. ( I guess). Flight was from Philadelphia to Ft Lauderdale. There was certainly no extra room involved. I selected a window and middle seat. Row 14. Boarding was a nightmare. They board in groups 1-8. You have to pay $34.00 in order to board in an early group. Just selecting an "extra room" seat for 2 people adds over $100.00 minimum to your cost. Otherwise you board, NOT from back to front, but apparently when you bought your ticket. You are allowed a carry on. except if you are in boarding groups 7 or 8. At the gate you will be told that if you are in groups 7 or 8, you must check your carry on.(Happens on full or nearly full flights). Since you selected a window seat you expect a window. Not on American. They jam so many rows on to the plane that about 30% of the window seats don't actually align with a window, so you are jammed against a blank bulkhead. No seat back entertainment. I am 6'1", so I don't consider myself overly tall. My knees were jammed against the seat in front of me, to the point where I could not really even access the seat pocket in front of me. The tray table was up against my chest. Not a great way to fly for 3 hours. For the way you get treated by this airline, you might as well fly Spirit or some other budget carrier and save on the fare. There is NOT comparison between this airline and competitors Delta, Jetblue, and United. Never again.

Very poor seats that are too close together with 30" claimed pitch seemingly a dream.  I am 6'1" (185cm ) tall and could not sit straight. Seats at the window e.g. 9A/ 14A etc. are even worse. My knees and behind were very sore after both flights of 4.5 -5.5 hrs. each. No chance to rest or sleep too uncomfortable made worse by the fact that both flights were virtually full. Food is poor and expensive with only water and tea/coffee free. Staff were friendly and good Flights left on time ands were trouble free - but those seats! Do not fly Virgin Economy if you are tall

Really poor seats for a 6 hour flight, along with the price I paid, offered only an uncrowded ambiance tho little comfort. There is no way to get rest as the seat recline is limited. Never again! I suggest that you Do not fly the Panama / Brazilia route as these are small planes. Come to think of it as Brazilia is the capital of Brazil it would be a nice change to have a lie flat seat - or almost - for the almost 6 hour flight to Panama. I feel the airline should I advise the passenger of the limited offering on these flights. Time for a change?
My seat (71J) was terrible. There was 2 black boxes fixed under the seat before me leaving me only 60% of the space that my feet would have had if I had been sitting in different row.

The seats are cozy and it can recline to a full flat bed, bedding and pillow are soft. The business class has a 1x2x1 configuration and my seat was assigned on the right hand of middle section. It has ample personal space and storage. It has decent privacy as there is a divider in the middle which separates me from the passenger on the left hand side. It would be nice if they can add sliding door in each business class seat like other airlines.

The 3x3x3 configuration on the A350-900 is desperately cramped. I have short legs but my knees were knocking against the seat in front and the 6 flights comprising my journey from London to Perth and return were spent with a neighbour's elbow poking into my side because of the narrowness of the seat and the armrest. Hard seats compounded the problem. No refresher towels or overnight comfort packs except a skimpy one on the outward leg on SA. Minimal food choice, and what was provided to me was inedible apart.

Comfortable seats with fairly good legspace compared to other low-cost airlines. There are no TV's or entertainment on board, nor are there any power supplies. The seats though are big enough and even though the seat in front of you reclines, you will not find a big difference in space.

I fly Munich to Cairo and back and, unfortunately was booked on this about 4-hour overnight flight. Lufthansa still uses the A321 with standard short haul seats which just recline a few degrees and make it impossible to get some sleep. In business class, the middle seat is blocked by a table. This makes it impossible to use the free seat as an extension of the already too small seat. So, although there was nobody sitting next to me, I still had to cram into my horrible flimsy seat. It was just torture. In Economy, people could at least use the other seats to lay down if there is nobody sitting there. After arrival, I had to go straight to work which was difficult as I did not get a minute of rest.

Swiss reminds me of a budget airline, similar to the European low cost carriers. Very narrow seats with very little leg space, maybe 28-29 inches. If you are over 6 feet tall, good luck. Every US domestic airline provides more leg space than our friends from Switzerland. A 3-4-3 seat configuration on a Boeing 777 says it all. I will definitely avoid them for international travel.

I tried the new A388 business class from London to Singapore. It was about 12-13 hours. My seat was 21K on the upper deck, along with the suites (the old ones used to be in the bottom deck). I think that the seat was pretty spacious for me (I'm 164cm) the footrest was good, but the legroom was to either to your left or right, which makes it quite uncomfortable. But on the SQ regional J class, its a straight legroom, so consider getting a 787-10/359 if you want a straight legroom. The bed couldn't recline fully into a flat bed, unlike the 773,359, the 388 uses buttons to recline the bed, it is done automatically, while the 773/359 is done manually. The table was pretty small compared to the 773/359 (hard to get out of your seat while the table is open) and some tables are also not fully functional, like mine, during landing the table popped back out, I have tried several times to push the table back in, but it just won't fully go in, it would still be loose. The crew was very kind, friendly and welcoming. They kept checking on me, which made me feel weird but happy in a way. I had 2 meals in total on this flight, lunch and supper/dinner. The lunch wasn't my favourite, the scrambled eggs were pretty basic. But the Dinner/supper, I love it, it was steak beef served with mash potatoes and a couple of vegetables, (not book the cook).

The seats on the way to Cancun from Mexico City were cramped, and the layout for all the seats was the same - first class and economy were no different. Checking in online from Cancun to Mexico City was a nightmare. First of all, you need the app and to register for their points program to check-in online. After that they gave my wife and me middle seats in different rows (I didn't pay for specific seats). Then I tried to change our seats and had to pay for "comfort" seats (same as economy but further forward) and was bombarded with attempts to sell me First Class seats (same as economy but further forward). When I paid for the "comfort" seats the payment "failed" for unknown reasons and so I tried again and the exact same seats were over double the price! The price increased by over double as soon as my payment "failed" for unknown reasons, and the comfort seats were now more expensive than the upgrade to First Class! Scammers! We'll just sit in different rows to Mexico City.

Whilst the leg room on the outbound flight to Calgary seemed adequate, the width of the seating wasn't. I was unable to use both arms to eat. Neither the persons either side of me were big, in fact they were both small ladies. Whilst the seating was ok for short internal flights the width of the seating is not adequate for long haul. I would not travel with this airline again.
Wide and comfortable with enough legroom. Clean, perfect level of recline. Headphone and control point on the seat. Seat covers were good and clean, looked new and properly maintained

It was a full flight. Not much legroom. We sit in the 4 seats row for easy access to the toilets. I’d recommend to pay extra legroom near the exit door rows. Flight attendant were nice. Inflight meal and entertainment was good.
I booked Qsuites and I got a 2x2x2 cabin configuration with angled bed, one of the worst trips of my life.
Resembles a low fare/low cost airline but with premium fares. Absolutely no difference. Any person taller than the average 1.75m will for sure have troubles to accommodate.

This seat is cramped. The pitch is 30-31 inches. The metal support from floor for seat in front is exactly in the space where you would naturally place your right leg, reducing the legroom significantly. I could not imagine siting in this seat for 12 hours, it would be torture. Luckily for me was a quick trip to Bangkok.

The seats are very narrow and big guy next to me extended several inches beyond. Most uncomfortable ride ever. the seats were redesigned recently to cram passengers. Love AA but now looking for more comfortable airline for international travel. 17" seats doesn't cut it!

Seat was ok, can't say comfortable really. Unfortunately the inflight entertainment system wasn't working for me and my family ( 4 seats) we weren't given any alternative seats and when I got back to the gf customer support - they only had an apology concerning the in-flight entertainment and told me that they will forward to relevant department. I regret choosing gulf air. Even the customer support wasn't satisfactory - when I replied to them with my concerns in the emails - the support wrote to me in the 2nd email that he/ she doesn't want to elaborate further... we faced flight delay and no in-flight entertainment on our seats - really sad. Such service is not expected and not satisfied at all

Flew PR119 flight from Toronto to Manila, 16-hours of uncomfortable sitting in a Business Class seat. The seat buttons did not function so the seat was immovable, finishing the journey with a neck pain and sore back. The inflight Chief Purser stated that this is an ongoing issue with the airline and the airline isn't rectifying it.

Flight attendants and active flight staff are fantastic, however customer service and seat design is atrocious. I ended up collapsing on the flight and had to be walked off by emts, tried to change my return ticket to another member of my family as its clearly unsafe for me to fly and the fee was insane. Basically would have been buying a new ticket. Now to the seats on the flight, if you in anyway have a medical condition that is triggered by positional sensitivity then frontier is NOT for you. You cannot lean forward to put your head on the tray and you can in no way shape or form lean back. In order to restore my blood pressure I have to be reclined or supine-neither of which are remotely possible on a frontier flight. Ended up laying on the floor (which left black marks on all my clothes as the floors were very dirty) in front of the bathroom because there is no safe place on this plane in case of medical emergency. Also the space between passengers is non existent-as a 120lb 5’10” extremely slender woman I was absolutely eclipsed by the two passengers on either side of me. Flight attendants 10/10, passenger comfort and humanity of customer service- 0/10.

I was initially worried about that older AA product and concerned that seating backward might be uncomfortable. It turns out that I prefer seating backward in lie flat position because of the angle of attack of the plane. Your head remains above your feat and it feels better. I also enjoy the fact that the seat does not have a footwell which usually feels cramped. On the other AA B777 seat configuration I keep banging my knees at the top of the footwell when I move. There is consequently a little less storage available but I prefer the openness of the pod configured that way.

We were in seats 33A and 33C - would highly recommend these seats as they are the last seats in premium economy section with a bulkhead behind which allows you to have the seat reclined whenever you like without interfering with passengers behind you. The first row seats in premium economy s 31 similarly have no seating in front as on exit row but TV screens are either mounted in between the seats in a centre console or on the bulkhead in front, excellent legroom but screen position could be an issue.

Travelled business class in from LON to BLR on 28th oct and absolutely worst experience on business class. Small and cramped seats, less space and weird sitting arrangement., had to turn my head almost 180 degree to see outside window while seating on the window seat. Virgin Atlantic had the worst business class experience. I could literally peep in my front and back seats, no privacy at all.

Being a normal sized guy...5'9" and 165lbs., I was reasonably comfortable on board the 2 flights, both in the 4 hour range. Seats were what I get on most commercial flights I have taken over the past decade. I had 7H (aisle) on the way up and 14c (aisle) on the return. 14c is a great seat and I will book that again! Personally, no complaints from a seasoned flyer.

I had booked 6 Business class tickets and was seated in the 11th row, however, one of them was defective and wouldn't recline. The crew tried to fix it to no avail. They highlighted that the plane is full and confirmed that 2 other seats of "staff confirmed booking" refused to swap with a full paying customer. I paid nearly AED14,000 per ticket! To compound things further, the service was horrendous, the head stewardess had an extremely bad attitude and they didn't even serve me my order until i went to inquire about it because they forgot. The Purser threatened me to delete the footage of the malfunctioned chair otherwise she would notify security to meet me upon landing. This is what it has come down to with what used to be one of the best airlines in the world. Daylight robbery, bullying, and a snobby attitude!

A major fatal flaw in the terribly designed business class seat which is truly awful if you want to try to sleep! While it’s a flat bed you are forced to sleep diagonally with very narrow footwells so that if you want to change position to lie on your side then your other side it’s impossible! It’s to restrictive to move so you’ll hardly get any decent sleep unless you have consumed large amounts of alcohol from the great choice on the wine list - whoever designed this seat needs to be fired! Apparently talking to one flight attendant they did say there’s a refit of new seats & interior on this aircraft planned but wasn’t sure when. Seat adjustment controls worked if you hold & press, which is a bit outdated & needs improvement. lighting was sufficient for reading. Privacy on an aisle seat is never any good so if that’s what you want then window seat is recommended. So A380-800 business class seat not recommended & if you want a good nights sleep & opt for the A350 or 777 aircraft with Singapore.

A320 NEO with new design and bigger overhead bins, seat new and comfortable. seat pitch on my seat (27H Aisle Seat) was 32 inch. Seat very comfortable. For travelling in Economy class on narrow body aircraft was a very great comfort.
Seat were pretty comfortable, adjustable head part. the blanket on the seats were also comfortable. seats are wider because of the 2X4X2 composition.
Seat 57g aisle seat must have been one of the most threadbare and uncomfortable seats i have ever had the misfortune to be seated on. Food was way below par from what it once was.

I usually flew them on the LGW-ATH and ATH-LGW route and I did so on a repeat basis. They served this route with a A321 but they switched aircraft last minute. Their aircraft  are extremely tight legroom wise but I flew them on the basis that I prebuy extra legroom seats in an exit row which cost 25 euros. They advertised the seats on row 12 as exit row and extra legroom. However, on 3 occasions, they changed their aircraft to a A320 for operational reasons and reseated me in seats which cost the same but were not extra legroom. The first two occasions I called their customer service and I was able to reseat myself in a row with extra legroom. In the third occasion, for which I am submitting this review, they changed the aircraft to an A320, reseated me to 4F, which is not extra legroom. They did not notify me beforehand and did not provide me any options. I found out at checkin. I called their customer service before departure and I explained that I could not fly with their limited legroom and requested that they change my seat. They were not able to accomodate me as the plane was full. I said I could not fly in this case and I explained I wanted resolution to the matter before takeoff so that they dont deem my absence as a no show. They did not offer to change my date or do anything. They instead told me to email them with the circumstances implying I could get my money back. When I emailed them, I did not receive a response for a month. They ignored me. When I pestered them again, I received a response that this was a "no show" and I could not be reimbursed except for taxes and as a favor for the seat charge. They advertise seats as extra legroom and change them without having explicitly rules about doing that. They have since changed the indication "extra legroom" in those seat but have left it in when you click in it (see attachment). Second, they did not notify me in time and give me options. Third, I called to make changes before departures but they led me to believe that I would be reimbursed instead of telling me that I would be losing my money as a no show (I probbed them on this matter). This level of service is not acceptable.

The aircraft looked very old from its interiors. The legroom was good for economy class. The seat was old, the screen was not working, tray table was in bad shape, I virtually had to hold it with one hand while having meals with the other. The charging slot was broken. Screen was not working.
Extremely cramped, seats were very thin and had no padding. Very little room for my feet under the seat in front as well. Made worse when seat in front was reclined. Food choice was very poor

Their business class in the A380 is average in the 777 is terrible at best. Seats are bad! Food is so bad! Lounges are bad. Their business model to make money definitely works, their experience is horrendous

Seat width and legroom is reduced to a minimum. If you are above 1.90m you won’t be able to fit in without touching the front seat, especially if the person in front of you lowers it to have a sleep. Same for your feet if you try to fit them below the front row. I almost had more space in my following short haul connecting flight with old A320. The table is ridiculously small. There is not enough space to store basic items with you : water bottle + phone + wallet and the seat pocket is overfilled. A detail compared to the seat comfort, but despite the plane being brand new, inflight entertainment system does not allow personal Bluetooth earphones connection.
Seats in economy are quite comfortable, I could strech my legs , more or less (I am 180 cm). Space between seats is good. Very comfortable seats and very good reclining.

The seats are confusing. They do not match the outside row. 22 window seats match to 21 center row. Several people sat in the wrong seat — me too. Also center row seats E & G straddle a bar supporting the seat in front. So my underseat bag was placed weirdly, partly on my neighbors feet. The seats are narrower than the seats in my first leg of this trip. Otherwise its airy and as is customary - a half pinky finger biscuit with a beverage. Service is excellent!

When reserving the ticket, I have paid for seat selection and selected window seat (7A) for 12€ surcharge. There was no window in that row on that side of the plane. And as the plane was fully booked, I couldn’t change my seat after boarding it. The lack of the window in the seventh row was never mentioned during the reservation process, nor it was on the drawing during the seat selection.

Absolutely ridiculous leg room. I'm fairly tall, but have never encountered this on an intercontinental flight of 9 hours. This was pure torture. If I wasn't sitting next to the isle (which was also shockingly narrow, by the way!), I simply wouldn't have been able to sit, period. I could not move whatsoever and was in pain after a while. This is totally unacceptable and needs to be dealt with TUIfly! Never again.

Copa Airlines is very helpful, especially with seat assignments. I bought a last minute trip due to the fact that I had a very painful lumbago and I need to go back to the doctor ASAP. I called the customer service rep to request a wheelchair service for next morning since I could not walk and she added it without hesitation. The next morning I went to the airport to take the flight and, since I bought a last minute ticket my chair was 33C, the last row, really difficult to access for someone who cannot walk, and the rep issued me a better seat, 5D, really comfortable. In Panama, as well, they noticed my impairment and issued me 5F, really comfortable for my back. My special thanks to all the reps In Orlando and Panama who made this painful trip more tolerable; special thanks to Kimberly Martinez en Panama who got me a last minute comfortable chair. Because of this and punctuality of the schedules I highly recommend Copa Airlines.

Extremely uncomfortable seat due to the sunken seat cushion and lack of lumbar support for a five hour flight from JFK to PHX. My spouse had the similar complaint. JetBlue used to offer one of the most comfortable seats. What happened?

The seat is quite comfortable and has good legroom, there is good space on the window seats, the IFE is outdated though and you can't adjust the angle of the head rest. The window is very big and your receive some sort of service every 1-2 hrs.

I was very excited to fly on this brand new configuration of the A320 Neo. We all know Spirit crams you in and for this particular flight I was on the middle seat, luckily for me I was traveling with two family members so we had the entire row and it was not that uncomfortable sitting in the middle because on each side I had family rather than strangers. This was supposed to be a five hour flight from Philadelphia to Las Vegas that turned into a seven hour flight due to taxi delays at takeoff and once we landed. Those seats by no means are designed to be seated on for more than 4 hour maximum. I am 5’9” 150lbs so it was not a matter of not fitting in the chair but a matter of virtually no padding. Your lower back and legs begin to get num after 3 hours sitting on pretty much a plastic seat. Not sure Spirit will improve this but be aware that unless you can afford to upgrade to a Big Front Seat it will be brutal to fly on a regular seat for more than 3 hours. Heading back to Philly I’ve already secured a Big Front Seat so look out for that review. Like I do on all my Spirit Airline reviews, they do not claim to be the most comfortable or service orientated airline. They take you from point A to point B safely and for this flight they did just that.

This flight from Philadelphia to Frankford was a little bit over eight hours so I upgraded to Lufthansa‘s premium economy. The row of seats right behind the last row in business has more legroom than other premium economy rows on the A330-300. The seat was very comfortable, plenty of storage, two windows, great entertainment.
Very comfortable seats with ample legs room. Foot rest was helpful for long flight. Food was served with napkins for food trays. Overall I find seating arrangement very good.

Flying from JFK to Nairobi. Tried to upgrade my economy seat to business via Kenya Airways online bid system (offered several days before the flight), but my offer of $1700 per ticket was declined. I ended up pay a slight premium to move into bulkhead seats (25g & h), which was a great decision. These seats face the lavatory, which wasn’t an issue at all, and provided us with endless legroom. The seats are an exit row, so the armrests are fixed, but I did not feel the seat width was cramped. The seat recline is pretty decent, and the cushion extends out with the recline, so you can get yourself into a pretty acceptable position to sleep. The only downside is the seat cushions felt pretty thin/hard, so after a few hours you could start to feel a little bit of an ache. Overall, this was an acceptable option and probably worth the $3,400 I saved on my i upgrade bid since Kenya Business class is not really on par with other Asian/Mid-East carriers. Overall it was a good flight.

In September we took our first Business Class flight for a couple of years returning from Samoa on QF340. With a flight time of 6.5 hrs and late arrival into Sydney, we were looking forward to the extra comfort and service. We had seats 5E & 5F located next to each other in the center of the aircraft. The seat design is an insult to passengers travelling together, the idiot who designed these seats has no idea about the needs of travelling companions. You are separated by a fixed “divider” making it almost impossible to see each other and have any form of conversation. My wife is an anxious flyer due to an experience with an emergency landing which almost had a fatal outcome for all on board. Being separated like this made it very difficult for her, I spent half the flight on the edge of my seat leaning around the “divider” so I could talk to and console my wife who was stressed throughout the flight, very uncomfortable. Economy Class would have been so much better. There was no welcome drink or an amenities kit – where has the Qantas standard gone! For dinner we were served roast chicken that was inedible, tough and chewy! No entrée and the little dessert cake came in a paper box. After eating half of the dessert, I stopped due to a piece of the paper lining coming free and ending up in my mouth – disgusting! My wife didn’t touch her dessert. Why are we paying extra for this rubbish, had better meals in economy. While the seat and food proved to be a huge disappointment, the staff were very friendly and attentive. Being a “gold for life” Frequent Flyer, I have experienced many O/S business class flights over the past 25 years but this was the worst, never again – Qantas has totally lost the plot!! When we go to Europe next year, it will be on another airline.

We had a trip to Dublin from Orlando Fl from 09/21/2022 to 09/29/22 (direct flights). It took me 5 different phone calls (due to excessive wait times) to get seat assignments with extra legroom, but finally secured them. On our outbound flight, the seats were not worth the extra cost - I'm 5'4" tall and my knees were hitting the seat in front me. So little room that you can't even bend down to get your bag from under the seat in front of you. When we arrived in Dublin we discovered that my husbands bag never made the flight - we had checked in 2 1/2 hours before the flight. He did not receive his bag until Tuesday - our flight was on the previous Thursday/arriving Friday morning - that's four days. Their online baggage claim portal site that is supposed to keep you updated on the status of your bag was never once updated - again multiple phone calls had to be made. The fun wasn't over yet, our return flight on the 29th was cancelled. This was due to the hurricane in Florida, so we didn't blame the airline at all, but what we did have a problem with is that we never received a single email or notification of this - I checked the flight status on their website. We were automatically rebooked on a flight from Dublin to London, but with no way of getting from London to Orlando. Again, we had to call them to make the changes. We were rebooked on a flight from Dublin to Newark to Orlando (this leg was on United airlines because Aer Lingus could not accommodate us). On the 7 1/2 hour flight from Dublin to Newark we were given even worse seats than the flight over, less legroom if you can believe it, and the seats did not recline the whole cursory 3/4 of an inch normally allowed. Long story short, this airline needs to get its act together, and airlines as a whole need to be regulated for the amount of space to be provided to economy class passengers. Not everyone can afford the extra $1000+ for business class seats.
Not much to say other than comfortable enough, good legroom and clean, met expectations for short haul and was comfortable for a 2 hour flight not much more to comment on!

Seating is very uncomfortable.  Sleeping configuration is not comfortable. You need to sleep on an angle sticking your feet in a small hole. The seat is lightly padded. Food is low quality for business class and no longer offers a rich Peranakan mix, but a Chinese bias. Media system resets when any connected device detaches and reattaches. Book the chef food never got loaded.

The advantage of the shell type seat is that nobody will recline and hit your knees. However if you are tall, they are not very comfortable for an 11 hour flight. The In-flight entertainment Entertainment System is of very good quality, even on dated 777 aircrafts

Seats are definitely on the cramped and tight side on a 3x3x3 configuration in the economy class. If you want a comfortable seating position to rest and even take a nap, recommend picking the window seats, it has slightly more space. On the good side, aisles are slightly wider than the 3x4x3 configuration in some other aircraft types, so passengers should be able to walk down the aisle comfortably. The in-flight entertainment screen is awesome and every seat houses a USB charging port, which is somewhat rare in economy class despite more airlines begin to offer that.

Great experience on Eva Air. I travel a lot for work and company policy only allows for PE on long haul. EVA Air was a cut above on this leisure trip from Singapore to Vancouver via Taipei. Seats were very comfortable, the service was super professional and friendly, with the cabin crew very attentive. Some of the key differences over other airlines PE offering, was the supply of a proper and good quality amenity kit by Furla; plus a dedicated bathroom for PE customers. Also the food was really high quality and more like a business class offer than economy. My only criticism would be the IFE entertainment choices in English, which were comparatively limited. All in we had a very comfortable trip, with great service at a very reasonable price. I would travel with them again without hesitation and definitely in preference to Singapore Airlines, where routes allow.

Narrow seats make an uncomfortable long haul flight. Service was okay, food is also good. But the biggest drawback is simply the cabin. Regardless the snazzy façade with wooden divider accent, mellow mood lighting theme, the 17.05" wide economy seat on 777-300ER is too awful when the seats are fully occupied. Bumping shoulder is expected, having to dislodge someone next to you from their seats when you try to find your seat belt or reach to your pocket is inevitable. They don't even try to make amends by increasing the pitch. It is just a meagre 32". As a small 5'9" (175 cm) person, it feels cramped already when the passenger in front of you reclined their seat. Cannot imagine using this aircraft to flew to LAX from TPE. Not worth anything beyond $50 per hour of flight, as the seat comfort is not any better than low cost carrier in their 737NGs (just slightly above 17").

We went from Berlin to Doha in Business Class. The seats were clean and comfortable but felt a bit small. Every seat was equipped with its own sliding door. The seat was not one of QR’s famous QSuite seats. There was an Iphone holder with integrated charger which I found very useful. The socket was not working properly. There was not a lot of storage room, so I had to put my shoes in the overhead compartment. All together, this was a pleasant flight which felt a bit “corporate”.
Poor Economy class seating. Very small, no legroom and soft back seats, so you can feel passengers kicking you during the flight. No entertainment systems.

Awful seats on the A330. Very uncomfortable legroom for a long haul flight from Istanbul to Bangkok. This had to be similar to a low cost airline's legroom and is not in the same league with any other airline. Utterly disappointed with this airline and I've had several bad experiences with Turkish Airlines a few years ago. Terrible legroom, seats were uncomfortable and dated (over 10 years the cabin is and starting to show its age) I will no longer fly Turkish Airlines for long haul and would be better off flying on 5 star airlines for long haul travels like Singapore Airlines, ANA, and Qatar Airways in the future.

XXL seat with extra-legroom situated at emergency exit (rows 12 and 13). Non-reclining. The extra space is good for tall people. The seat can be reserved either for a fee or as part of a package (privilege pass) valid for one year on all Wizz flights. It is also possible to pay directly to the cabin crew if seat is still available (the fee is € 20 if paid in the aircraft).

The seats were horrible! For an 11 hour flight, you'd think the airline would provide an aircraft that's comfortable. The seats were narrow, very little cushion and uncomfortable. We even paid an additional $83 each to upgrade to premium seats. What a waste of money. Pay a little more and fly in comfort, especially when flying overseas or for such a long period of time.

I had a window seat 15A. The seat cushion was rucked so it was impossible to sit comfortably. The window curves inward which seems to reduce further the limited knee room. SI still would recommend the airline as others who are under 5'8 won't be aggravated, and the seat cushion issue was presumably a rare occurrence?

If you want a seat you have to pay 30euros - we paid 4 seats round trip so 240€. None of our initial seat allocation was respected. The day before flying, they allocated us in the middle of aircraft. They should have informed us and refunded window seats. After calling, we had to go to the airport first to renegotiate our paid seats - my claustrophobic father was really stressed out thinking about not seeing outside. They removed us from our seat to gather a family of 7 people. But they changed all allocation to give what we paid for. On the trip back to Paris, I checked in online and get our paid seats (row 38 - same as 1st flight). I initially asked for those seats to be free to apologize for their first mistake but they never answered. However, we were given boarding passes with row 27 next to toilets instead of 38. I again needed to go and ask to change everything. I complained on the 5th December to get a refund for the seats and I remained 84 days without any answer. They guarantee and answer within 72h. On departure day, I did not sleep all night because my father was scared (first time he flew) - we had to go to the airport at 7am instead of 9am as we wanted - so we paid night taxi fare to be early because when i called day before they could change our allocation. On flight return they also change allocation. They will tell you they are able to do it regarding their safety policy etc, but on the full flight our seats are not located at emergency exit so no safety reason. To conclude : do not pay any seat because you will start dreaming about Polynesia but it will start and end by a nightmare with seat allocations. Luckily food and flight attendants were great. Booking and reservation and leaders for seats allocation need to be trained. I have never seen a company changing seats allocation. I know 5 other people who faced same issue, and I read here that i am not the only one.

United's Economy Class seating may be tight, and it can be challenging for someone taller than me. But the inflight entertainment is terrific, and the power supply is a mixture of plugs and USB ports.

I recommend sitting in rows 6 and 7 on Icelandair's 737 aircraft. There is better legroom than in seats at the rear of the aircraft and the screens are on the seatback, rather than in the seats in row 5, which are in the armrest and quite small. I recommend avoiding selecting seats in row 5 of Icelandair's B737 aircraft.

The worst business class seats we have experienced among the ones we have flown so far (UA, AA, ITA, AF, BA and KLM). Congested cabin, a 2-2-1 and 2-1-2 layout. Cramped 5 seats in a row where everyone else in their aircraft class has 4 seats! Seats are narrow, uncomfortable and the couple's seat by the window lack ANY work space area and minimal storage. The dining tray is a primitive design of a pullout from the small divider between the seats. The shoulder belt cuts right into your neck as 2 FA's admitted to this defective design! There is zero privacy on the isle seats.

BA doesn't seem to understand why its customers choose to fly with them over low-cost carriers like Ryanair, easyJet or Wizz Air and the keep racing to the bottom, despite never being cheap enough or comprehensive enough in terms of flights to certain destinations. They've installed the same appalling slimline seats easyJet and Wizz Air have, but managed to make them even more uncomfortable. They have no lumbar support, and also don't have headrests like BA's old Pinnacle seats. They also have no recline and despite being refurbished had no at seat charging either. My understanding was that seats upto row 12 should have the old Pinnacle seats, so I woke up early to check-in just as check-in opened on the app 24hrs before and was pleased to bag a seat in row 10 which should mean I have the old Pinnacle seat. Apparently not, at least not on BA Euroflyer their subsidiary at Gatwick, the whole plane had the new appalling slimline seats even in Business - I'd have been pretty appalled if I had paid extra to fly in that cabin and been left with that seat for 3hrs. They are probably ok for an 1 maybe 2hr flight max, but on a 3hr flight to Catania from Heathrow it was painful and we were left with a horrible back pain.

2 seats were allocated to me & my wife in the new A350 where both seats were not reclining. The ground staff was unaware & did nothing to sort the issue. Similarly on my flight from Delhi to Sydney on 11 May24, one seat had the same reclining issue. Air India management needs to have a good look to improve its reputation on customer services ... sorry state of affairs...

I purchased an extra space seat. Just before take off, the passenger seated next to me showed up with a very large dog. The dog was on leash but not in a container. I asked to be reseated but this was not possible as the plane was full. The dog continuously entered my space and disturbed my comfort; I had to constantly reposition my feet. I have asked for a refund but received various explanations regarding good will and liability but the answer remained no.

As it's a scheduled airline, there's little you can really say is special about the seat. It looks good, and the red ambiance is surprisingly calming and friendly on the eyes (especially at night). We purchased extra legroom which was a necessary for someone tall, standard legroom looked acceptable but tight for anyone wanting a comfortable flight despite being short haul. The seat was also relatively padded and supportive so that once I reached the destination, I was comfortable.

Sat in seats 24a outbound to Budapest and 18A return flight from Bucharest. Seats were both very worn and had a ridge running a couple of inches from the rear. My backside was numb on both flights and less than 3 hours for each flight. Legroom far to little for a national carrier. Also on the return flight the seat pocket had a hole at the bottom and only found this out when i put items in it and they fell on the floor and due to the lack of space had to ask fellow passengers if they could reach my stuff which they kindly did. USB charger  going very intermittent as well. I will avoid British Airways on short haul flights if possible.

Online booking and check in was easy but having flown numerous times previously from Gatwick to Toronto and Air Transat has gone downhill. It seems the seat area is smaller equivalent to Easyjet in the UK. I'm 5ft 10" medium build and struggled.. Anyone overweight will not only be extremely uncomfortable but make other passengers suffer. Is the 3x3x3 seating normal on a 330 Airbus? The food was pretty awful. Ok so it's a budget airline and costs are tight, l get that but don't expect much and you're be fine. Just not as it was.

Seat 16A on PSA Airlines’ CRJ-900 is an excellent choice, especially for a short flight like DCA to PHL. Positioned by one of the emergency exit windows, it offers plenty of legroom, making it one of the roomier seats on the aircraft. After a quick and straightforward briefing from the flight attendant—where I agreed to assist in the unlikely event of an emergency—we were on our way. While PSA’s CRJ aircraft are slightly smaller than those operated by other regional carriers in the same market, they are well-suited for the short hops PSA primarily flies. The seat itself was extremely comfortable, and for a 27-minute flight, I couldn’t ask for more. A solid choice for anyone looking for a bit of extra space on a quick journey.

They changed the aircraft from an A330 to a 737-800 and the seats must have been for short haul flights of two hours or less, as the 5 hour and 40 minute flight I endured was on the most uncomfortable seats I have experienced. The other story is trying to get a refund for the seat location we paid for, but we’re bumped from after they changed the plane type.
The most uncomfortable seats. I am a small person and I still felt claustrophobic, which is unusual for me on flights. The seats were very uncomfortable, after 30 minutes it hurt to sit.

May 2025 brought with it a refresh to the American Airlines B787 fleet, as part of this refresh it included new seat cushions to the economy cabin seats. These were to provide ‘extra comfort’, unfortunately the rigidness of the foam provides very little noticeable ‘comfort’ apart from the thickness difference which brings new problems for taller or larger passengers. As someone over 6ft, my comfort comes into question if my shoulders go above the headrest, or the armrests are too low for my elbows to rest comfortably on them. The extra thickness of these new cushions caused exactly that, I was unable to fold the headrest wings because I was sat too high for the highest headrest setting, my thighs were above the armrests and so my elbows only reached them if I slouched awkwardly. The final issue I had is I had to pull the seatbelt out to its full length, usually I have about 6-8inches of slack on the seatbelt. I dread to think what a larger passenger would do, risking the need for a seat belt extender! American needs to revert to the old 2 inch thick seat cushions, these ones were a bad decision.

We recently travelled Auckland - Singapore -London - Singapore - Auckland, on both the A350 and B777. Service was perfect, as usual, and food quality was generally good.Entertainment seems to have declined. The great disappointment was the Business Class seat, same on both aircraft. It cannot be fully reclined without conversion to a bed, and to put your feet up requires twisting diagonally into a barely comfortable position. Not much better when fully flat in bed form. I have travelled on Singapore business and first over almost 30 years, and this seat is the worst i have experienced.
Extremely narrow seats, and not very comfortable in terms of reclining, tray size and placement, and seat cushioning. The leg room was decent.

Recently flew with Air Transat from London to Toronto, and it was one of the worst flight experiences of my life. Flight attendants totally inattentive. I sat next to the aisle and my shoulder was hit hard over 10 times by the flight attendants without so much as an "Excuse me" or "Sorry".  The headphone jack on the entertainment system was broken so could not use the system to watch movies. No individual air valves to control temperature at your seat so I was cooking on board the flight.The tray table was broken so when the flight attendant put the meal on the table, it slid off into my lap.  Called Air Transat to help resolve the issue, I asked to give us 1 free checked bag on the return leg home to compensate for this ordeal and the answer was no.

LH A350-900 business class configuration is somewhat funny trying to give window access to all side seats; as a result, the individual cabins felt claustrophobic and surprisingly uncomfortable, both as seats and as beds. The seats are relatively narrow and barely long enough, which was all right for me but may be a real issue for bigger passengers.

Literally the smallest width seats possible. Sitting in the seat and the arm rest can't even go fully down. I'm 6'2", 220lbs. The oppression next to me weighs more and has an even wider hip span. We are sitting on top of each other to fit in the seats.

We were a family of five, and our seats were one middle row plus one seat on the middle-left aisle in front of the middle row we occupied. Seat was comfortable and came with blanket, pillow and pair of headphones and toys for children. The IFE system is the best of airlines we’ve travelled. Most of the content on the system is in English, but there are options in other languages. TV is large. Selection of entertainment for kids was excellent. All seats with a USB port and most seats also with a three-prong electrical socket. Storage space for baggage is ample. Legroom is sufficient for tall passengers.

I hadn't flown for quite a few years, and this trip to Jamaica and back was the worst experience for seating I have ever had. To have to upgrade to board first is ridiculous. We were in group C with grab any seat that is left splitting up your party. With that said there is no managing of the seat arrangements. So with 3 seats on each side, couples will take the isle seat and window seat with their carry on's in the center seat and not willing to give it up. My daughter had to argue with a man on the plane about it. Fortunately his girlfriend moved to the center seat. There were other unhappy people that ran into the same situation. The open seating is fine but needs to be managed better. If at all possible I will NEVER fly this air line again. At least assigned seating you knew you had a seat and didn't have to grapple for one, AND majority of the time you wouldn't be splitting up the party you are with. Very unhappy about this part of my trip!

I chose one of the Scoot Stretch seats, Row 1, seat C. I can highly recommend. This seat gave me the benefit not only of extra leg room, but also it was very quiet being far away from the engines. As well as this, I was one of the first on, and first off of the flight. Ample room for my 6'3" frame. I would say though, that the seat could probably use a little extra padding on the bottom part. I have worked in aviation, and I know that all the time airlines are trying to cut down on aircraft weight so the flight is more economical. But please Scoot, don't do it at the price of the comfort of your customers. Flight was only three hours long. I was starting to get a little uncomfortable by then. I could have gone perhaps another two hours maximum. Despite this, this is a good seat and I can highly recommend.

It was my first time flying Flair airlines and I was really curious about what the ULCC would deliver. I had read all about their poor on time departure performance and customer service issues and was prepared for anything they threw at me. I have no complaints whatsoever. We did purchase the big bundle and had priority boarding so this we super smooth as well. I sat in their preferred section where there was extra legroom and felt is was also great - Seat 3F. My only complaint here is that this specific seat is narrower than others perhaps due to the shape of the fuselage. I would not recommend row 3 again. At least Row 4 if the Window seat is desired. And as expected we departed more than an hour later than scheduled. but overall a good experience. I would recommend them for leisure travellers who are not making any connection and really want the bare bones experience (no power, no entertainment).

IFE inconsistent and poor - if you end up flying on one of MAS' 737-800s that have not been refurbished or retrofitted for some reason, despite having a core fleet of 737-800 for a long time now, there won't be any inseat IFEs, even in business class. If you do get to board a "standard" 737-800, you'll find the IFE rather outdated and tedious to use, compared to other similar airlines. Endless clicking and scrolling just to look for movies/music/shows - very poor user interface and leads to passengers spending too much time holding the remote, which is not ideal given the current situation. Flight Info function was not working at all on one flight, which was inconvenient.

Virgin is back to a cheap low cost carrier offering like it used to be when it was Virgin blue. Uncomfortable seats where you can feel the rear passenger’s knee poking in your seat - buy your own food and drink except one free glass of water - NO usb or charging port, no entertainment you have to bring your own device to connect to their wifi entertainment, but no charging port?

Terrible and rock hard seats. It was a short to middle flight, but I think the seat could be a little bit more comfier. The crew service and onboard service was great, but the flight was very basic. No wifi and no onboard entertainment. When coming back home, I bought a larger seat, and it seemed to be a bit more comfier, but still uncomfortable.
Seat 13D is for me one of the best seat for this type of aircraft with legroom. You just have to accept the instructions to be followed for emergency exits.

Did research, premium economy, looks good with extra width seats more legroom and extra recline on the seats. We had a 20 hour red eye flight LHR to SYD with a refuelling and quick crew change in SIN. Looks deceive. We were seated in row E (middle 2 of 4) centre aisle. Great, until the seat in front reclined and we discovered we were trapped. The seat arms are not retractable, (that is where the tray table is located). The distance between the arm rest and the fully reclined seat in front is under 7 inches. To extract yourself you have to wake 3 passengers, 2 in front to lift their seat backs to an upright position and the passenger to your side to allow you to lift your legs up over the arm rests. I found it impossible to watch my screen due to it being so far off vertical, it was sending me dizzy looking at it. One other problem I discovered, because I was stressed at being uncomfortable I started getting hot to find the Boeing 777 does not have individual air conditioning cold air nozzles, once the temperature is set it can’t be individually cooled. On the positive side the food was good I did however miss the coffee pot after the meal.

Horrible seats, not comfortable at all. Dirty seats in business class. Definitely not worth the big price tag for thousands of euros. Avoid if you are looking for comfort or cleanliness over a flight. And the food is horrible.

Sitting in those seats was the worst 16 hours of my life! I'm a tiny 5'3 frame and my shoulders were touching the two people next to me. One of them had their leg touching mine the entire time. I could not move my feet either because I had a bag stowed under the seat in front of me and there was no legroom left. The screen felt like it was right up in my face and there was hardly any reclining in the seats. The best part about the flight was going into the bathroom where I did not have to touch the person next to me or hear them breathe. I've been on many flights before including international ones with Cathay Pacific and never complained about the seats in economy. I heard they had condensed the seats a few years ago which is why the space was so small. I could tolerate a few hours flying like this, but 16 hours was well past my limit. Thankfully, I upgraded to Premium Economy flying back. The difference was day and night. I wasn't touching anyone and had plenty of legroom. Even as a budget traveler, it was worth every penny. Never again, Cathay Pacific.

Night flight from PVR to YVR. 5 hour duration, departing 2100. All seats are permanently locked upright with no choice to recline at all. It simply punishes its passengers in doing this with no real common sense at all, especially on a night flight.

The massage function on this seat did not seem to work well, felt hardly any movement. It was very comfortable whilst seated upright. Once the seat was reclined, and the foot well was very tight. I did not have a good night. A full breakfast was offered after take-off (almost midnight Sydney time). Strangely not many passengers accepted. Prior to landing a light meal was offered. I was asked every time I used the toilets whether I was a business class passenger. The paper towels in the bathroom were so thin it dissolved in wet hands. The lounge was Premium Plaza Lounge and I would not pay good money to use it. Food was limited, the pasta was congealed and the cakes/desserts was dry from sitting too long on display.
Worst seat we have ever had to endure on a long haul flight. No room at all and not what we expected would not recommend this airline

Boeing 787-9 - not worth the money. The seats were extremely narrow so like lying in a coffin. When the seats were out (which is all the time on these long flights) you have to clamber over passengers to get to the toilet. The configuration of the cabin means that some one is always waking up someone else. This is an economy seat masquerading as a business class seat and is misleading and deceptive conduct because there is NO WAY you can get any rest if you book with British Airways.

Below standard business class seats despite new aircraft. Basically an Economy seat (42 cm Wide) fitted in a business class plastic shell with fixed armrests which cannot retract of be lowered. Arms devoid of support in bed position and so narrow that it makes you feel claustrophobic and squeezed in a narrow foot pit and plastic shell. No seat storage. Definitely not to standards and would not recommend. Boarding was hectic and delayed by more than 75 minutes without any announcement. The ground staff looked unprofessional.

Worst business class seat I’ve ever had. Very thin cushioning, not comfortable. Bed cover is not a mattress at all, just a thin piece of material. You can’t lie straight, you have to lie on an angle and rest your legs on the footrest with your feet in a small cavity. Very poor for a business class product, Avoid at all costs.

Good food, modern aircraft, poor service. To AA's credit, the food was good and plentiful. But the crew didn't care if I enjoyed the flight and didn't seem to enjoy their work. They actually seemed more like old, tired police officers whose main intent is to force compliance with the rules. Jaded, overworked, unsmiling, unhappy people who have made this trip thousands of times but for whom passengers seem like an impediment to ending the crew's workday. PA system was so weak that I could not hear the announcements. Also, the crew can control the window tint, which they kept blackened for almost the entire flight. That makes the window seats into dark, black holes which I will never intentionally use again. Infotainment system is awkward and unimaginative. 110v power outlet is very difficult to reach, hidden behind an armrest. Need to have more USB-C outlets. Work on the ground in Tokyo was handled by Japan Airlines staff, who worked hard and were presentable. Unless I'm using AA frequent flyer miles I will use JAL (or, for that matter, any other airline) for my next trip to Japan.

This was my 3rd roundtrip ticket with Saudia in the past 2 yrs, the previous flights were reasonable for the price paid, but these last 2 flights were very bad. I flew MNL - RUH - CDG. On the first flight from MNL I had booked seat 70L. Heard the crew saying: Are we ready for the movie marathon, while handing out the earplugs, or is it gonna be a sleeping marathon? Well, quickly most passengers found out the last would apply, because more then 75% of the screens didn't work. Sleeping for me was also not an option, because the recline also didn't function.  This B777 was in a real bad shape. The cabin crew member did give me another seat in the front of this cabin, but with the 3x4x3, try to eat all at the same time, rubbing elbows? There was nothing comfortable about this flight.  The flight to CDG, also a B777, but not much better then the flight from MNL. Here also most screens of the entertainment system didn't work and the USB ports also didn't function.

A premium flatbed seat for USD50 over a regular seat needed no convincing. Even though it wasn’t a complete 180° flatbed, it got to about 160° which was still pretty good and decent enough for some rest. I had no issues stretching out completely. Width, length and comfort were all very decent and well worth the upgrade. Pillows and blankets provided too.

I'm not a tall person, but I struggled to be comfortable I had 2 flights each way via Dubai. 7 hours to Dubai, then 9 hours plus to Narita, then 12.5 hours back to Dubai then 8 hours back to Glasgow. Unfortunately on the way out I could hardly move and I ended up getting Cellulitis which left me unwell and put dampener on the holiday. All seats I could hardly move , my lower back was constantly in pain which left me struggling to get off my seat even to go for a walk around the cabin, make things worse the seat was broke from NRT-DXB crew couldnt help and ICE System didn't work either, leaving me with a very bad Emirates experience.

I have never experienced such little legroom as on my latest Iberia flight MAD - MVD. Almost 13 hours flight but you get less legroom than on a low cost airline. The overhead storage is ridiculously small. Really disappointed in Iberia. Feel like it wasn’t this bad before.

Pleasant cabin layout. The screen size was excellent and the provision of power supply is also commendable. Good seat, legroom good enough for me, good recline and seat width also, access way is enough.

Seat looked comfortable but was not in fact. The colours were the typical Air India arrangement two peach/orange at window and aisle and one red in the middle. The recline was ok for the aircraft type but the cushion at back was all gone, it was almost hard plane surface, felt like sitting on a wooden chair. legroom was acceptable if not comfortable. width was not a problem for me as I am not too wide. seat base though was comfortable. No charging point was there, neither plugs nor USB, but was not a problem for a flight of little over an hour. TV screen was not available

Completely horrible seats. We booked and paid a fairly significant premium for allegedly extra seats in row 1DEF. A disgusting rip off by Jet2. These seats are appalling. If they provide extra legroom, it is a tiny amount and not worth the ridiculous rip off amount this increasingly third rate airline charges. Compared to Easyjet and they fail on every level except the crew. They are unfailingly pleasant and hard working.

Excellent pitch with plenty of space with good old-school quality comfortable reclining seats on an A330 . Same comfortable seating on my connect flight with B737 . My experience was very positive, following several previous trips with modern A320Neo's and A350/B787 and the seats with other airlines.

Recently flew BA’s nonstop between Boston and London on the A380. It is a massive airplane with a payload of over 500 passengers. Business class seating on this plane and on this route was not worth the $$ in my opinion. There were too many seats in each row making the seats narrower than those offered by other airlines. Most jumbo jets have a 1-2-1 configuration in business class; this plane had 2-3-2 and 2-4-2, twice as many seats in each row. This is particularly obnoxious if you are seated in the middle aisle because that means anyone seated in a window seat or in the middle seats has to crawl over an aisle passenger just to get to the bathroom and back. If you do so in the dark on an overnight flight, it is actually unsafe for you and that poor aisle passenger. Check the plane scheduled for the flight you want to take and if a 777 is offered, opt for that one. They are all equipped with Club Suites in Business now.

The seat comfort in Lufthansa's short haul Business Class does not deserve the name Business Class. The seats are the same as in Economy and the seat pitch is also very low. Service and meals on board, however, were good.

Seats A & C in row 2 Club Class. Flew from Montreal to Rome in the Club Class and worth every dollar. Had issues getting out at night with row in front reclined and people sleeping. Flew home in row 6 seats A & B. Wished all the way home on this 8 hour day time flight that we had splurged on a Club Class seating again. The economy seating was very small and the cushion was maybe 1 inch thick. The attendants were very good and polite.

Horrible 4.5 hours of travel. The economy seats have zero leg room. There was no in flight entertainment for such a long flight. First round of snacks was offered by purchase only. Then the cabin crew came with another round of complimentary snacks. But people had already bought stuff on the first round. Economy class seats are horrible. There is not room to move your leg or even recline the seat a little bit. I would definitely avoid travelling in West jet because I cannot afford anything more that Economy class and their seats are just horrible.
A very uncomfortable seat in what looks like a new plane. No reclining seats, uncomfortable cushion. Do not use this airline if seat comfort is important to you.
