Spirits new improved seats are not designed to fit most people comfortably. It took the rest of the day for my back and neck to feel normal. Forget sleeping, and sitting is barely tolerable. I will never fly Spirit economy again. I am giving a 1 because the program won't let me rate this a zero

The arrogance and disrespect for my daughter. On both flights she was bullied out of her window seat by a family looking to seat their children at the window. On the first flight a family took advantage of early boarding for families. Kate arrived to the window seat I booked her and found a dad on the aisle and his five year old kid in her window seat (maskless, btw). He said his kid wanted to sit next to the window. Then another man came up and told the father in the window seat that he was sitting in his seat. So the father moved across the aisle, leaving her in the middle seat between a stranger and a random 5 year old without a parent.  I paid for that seat for her. This family had the opportunity to do so as well. Kate didn't want to have to complain to the father or out loud to the flight attendant and make trouble. Kate was texting me all this from the plane. I found out later that during the ascent the father had to attend to his five year old so got out of his seat to do so. The flight attendants got mad. Said he couldn't leave his kid and insisted on getting everyone to their correct seat. Then this morning as she was boarding her flight, same thing happened. Different family. At least they asked her this time. They wanted to be seated together. Now she's on the aisle. I told her to tell the flight attendant but she has decided not to as she'd be stuck on the inside with their screaming baby. Why bother offering to pay for seats if none of it matters anyway? The flight attendants should have to demand everyone sits in seats that are unpaid for. Not have to rely on paying customers to sort it out. It's terrible how she was put in this situation. A tiny 16 year old on her first flights alone.

Very little legroom on the A319 (6’ 2”) but good legroom on a A320. Dark and old feeling cabin.  Small window which was low down and dirty. Noisy cabin from engines No recline on seat. Small tray table which hadn’t been cleaned.

Despite originally paying extra for an exit row we were allocated an up-front seat, and that was bad for us. I am just on 6ft tall and my knees were rubbing the back of the seta in front. This was an overnight flight and they was no way I could get comfortable enough to get any sleep. The room is so tiny that the tray tables can't be lowered all the way to allow you to put any drinks or meals on them. Thank goodness the person in front of me didn't/couldn't recline their seat!

Outstanding seats, Boeing 777-300 seats are very comfortable and the amenity kit along with the plush bedding, mattress and comforter was perfect for the long haul flight. The new 787 Royal Laurel class seats are very spacious and comfortable as well.

On both my Boeing 777 and Airbus Swiss Air flights, the seats in front of me reclined so far the entertainment screen was inches from my face. It was extremely claustrophobic and uncomfortable. I've flown on at least a dozen airlines and have never seen seats recline so far. I loved everything else about the airline but would not fly them again for this reason alone. I'm short so I can't imagine how bad it is for tall people.

Luckily wasn't a long flight. I'm 6 foot 3 or 191 cm. My knees were rubbing on the seat, had no room for getting my legs to stretch underneath and if i was leaning with my back on the seat was even worse so I had to use an inflatable neck pillow to overcome it. Design not human or at least tall human friendly.

I took a flight from Seoul to Singapore. I paid $56 SGD to select a seat with extra legroom. I chose 10A (window), but on check-in, they told me 10D was better because 10B/C were filled, while 10E/F were empty, so I could have the entire row to myself. What I did not count upon was that my extra leg room because a short-circuit for more than a dozen people to switch from the left aisle to the right aisle so that they could use the right aisle toilet, which was visible, while the left aisle toilet was blocked off by a curtain. This group included one guy shouting at me because my legs were in the way as they traversed the space in front of 10D/E/F. Food was ordinary. Movie was good. Staff were pleasant. If I'd been in seat 10A, I would have enjoyed the flight.

Booked extra legroom seats for me and my partner, especially since usual seat layout is well too cramped for a 6'2" man. Was allocated 1B and 1C which was fine. Except priority boarding which came with the allocation was nonsensical since everyone and his dog has to file past us to reach their seats. Plus the cabin crew seats are directly opposite and they're not comfortable either so my leg room got totally compromised during take off and landing, and by their backwards and forwards servicing all the other passengers during the entire flight. The two seats need to be positioned closer to the aircraft side to provide non-contact by the food, beverages, and duty free trollies - or else what's the point of paying for extra leg room? The crew were very polite but that didn't make up for a very uncomfortable flight when comfort was the very thing we paid extra money for. Budget should never mean discomfort.
On Thai VietJet flight VZ962 from BKK to DAD Seat 6A on an A320-214, the tray table was broken and unfortunately, the passenger in front decided to recline their seat.

The legroom and width comfort is about the same as the other A320 aircrafts. They are still considerably comfy but restricted for short flights. The aisle is also wide enough to walk pass thanks to its comparably wider aircraft.

I’m 6’6” 280 lbs, I sat in seat 14F on a flight from MCO Orlando to ALB Albany NY, legroom was awful, but I got to choose my seat unlike with southwest, slimline seats are not the worst but the seat back entertainment and free WiFi made up for legroom, it was sufficient for a 3 hour flight. Plus it’s JetBlue, they ranked lowest this year and I do not understand why, I checked in in less than 5 minutes at a kiosk in Orlando, no hidden fees, didn’t have bags so no extras and made it safe, how can you complain about JetBlue? There are far worse airlines in this country.

I flew Turkish Airlines Business Class on a Boeing 773 from IST-LHR (Aircraft: TC-JJS). The cabin was clean. And the seat was also clean. Storage places were available under the foot rest area, as well as the storage bins and on the side of the seat below the reclining controls. Power supply was available under the arm rest. Wireless headphones were also provided. The IFE was controlled through a remote which was conveniently placed under the seat compartment, It was responsive with minimal lagging considering this was a slightly older cabin. The seat itself was very wide and comfortable. And it reclined into a full bed. However this was a day flight. I had reclined into a rest position but not a bedtime one.  The only thing the aircraft lacked was a privacy screen which I would prefer on longer hauls.. An excellent experience, I would definitely fly it again
What business class? There is none. Same seats and same cabin and same toilets. Like economy. The seats so small and with less cushion that it was painful for a 5 hour flight.
Small spaces between the seats. The TVs not working or working poorly. The choices of food is limited, and they don't offer vegetarian options of meals. They just don’t care!

Flying PHX-LHR, so long flight. Seat 39H I am 6'1", 210 lbs, so not outsize. Appalling seat design. Very narrow (10 abreast in a B777 should be a crime against humanity). Seat cushion surprisingly high, and, worse, rises when seat is reclined, jamming the knees against the back of the seat in front, and ensuring legs cannot be stretched under seat in front, making sleeping OR working virtually impossible - I am writing this sitting sideways, with legs and laptop in the aisle. Seat power supply does not appear to work. I normally fly BA on this route. The difference in seat quality is off the scale. Never again on AA.

The best feature of the JAL Premium Economy product is the seat. Encased in a shell like in Business class, no one can recline into your space and when you recline to have a nap, your feet move comfortably under the seat in front of you - even when you have hand luggage there. This might be less comfy if you are super tall but regardless, the leg rest and footstool combo keep the legs elevated which means you can turn onto your side. Pillow & blanket were comfy and the headrest was moldable so I actually slept - and the first stretch was a 14 hour flight. The seat was not hard and the result was that I felt quite fresh after each flight as I could get some sleep.

The seat and more particularly the seat layout is really disappointing for such a modern aircraft. The business class cabin looks as though it was designed 20 years ago. There's no aisle access from the window seats, whereas pretty much any other business class cabin in the 350 provides aisle access to all seats. More frustrating, there's absolutely nowhere to store anything. I really get the impression that Lufthansa chose the budget seat and cabin layout for their 350s. It's a shame as the soft product is excellent. Friendly staff, excellent catering.

Seat 26 H and K. These are the only 2 seaters available on the plane. Very useful for couples. Acres of legroom is another plus factor. Downsides are lack of window and proximity to toilet and the queues for them at certain times.

The most uncomfortable seat encountered. Minimal padding, no lumbar support, extremely uncomfortable, for the 6 hour flight to Cairns from Singapore. Don't book, unless you want to be in extreme discomfort, and have back ache for a day or two after. I am 6 ft tall, slim and fit. I booked an exit row seat thinking it would be more comfortable, but the seat has a stub as an arm rest meaning it is about 13 inches wide in practice.

The new A320neo feels worse than an old A320. The colours give however a nice touch. The seat pitch was awful and actually borderline for someone who’s over 185 cm.  Food was simple and not great. I would strongly avoid changing at Athens airport. Changing planes for a non Schengen destination means leaving the security area and going through security again. This was not communicated beforehand.
One of the worst business class seats, tiny seat. The lay out of the aircraft is very cramped, the plane was very dirty, amenity kit awful, service in general, not so good.

This is undoubtedly the most uncomfortable airline seating we have ever endured. WestJet is obviously the Canadian version of Spirit Airlines here. The seats are too narrow, do not recline more than an inch, and there is no padding whatsoever. Worse than sitting in a lawn chair for five hours. I will do everything in my power to avoid this airline for the remainder of my natural days. Awful experience and never again.

Row 41 on the A321 is a very comfortable seat, however I did have to pay a premium for the upgrade. Not sure what airlines are doing these days, but there appears to be very little lumbar support on these seats. Fortunately nobody was sitting next to me, so I was able to pad things out with a few pillows that were not in use. Saved me from any discomfort for that seven hours of flight, but I'm sure that I could not have stood much more than that.

I recently flew American Eagle from DCA to PHL on Republic Airways, and I was particularly impressed with the main economy extra cabin on the E175. The seat design offers an exceptional level of comfort with plush cushioning and enhanced legroom, ensuring a surprisingly pleasant experience on the short 27-minute flight. The thoughtful ergonomic design of the chair made it easy to relax, even on a brief journey. Overall, a well-executed seating configuration that complements Republic Airways commitment to professionalism and efficiency.

Horrible seat. No storage space beneath seat or overhead because another passenger put their bag up there. Very small labels to identify which is the correct seat and the cabin crew don't bother to give directions. No legroom, power sockets or entertainment. Wobbly tray table. Armrest was sticky and seat had droplets on it. At least I wore dark clothing to hide it rubbing off.

BA used a configuration of 2x3x2 seats per row. I was seated in a middle, small, claustrophobic cabin in the middle with no air flow. Service was handled over a passenger seating on both sides and stepping to the aisle required jumping over another passenger.

Seats are hard as a rock, slanting downwards, permanent butt formations, but have extendable height and wrap around head rests. LCD screen is not user friendly. Seats seem to be wide enough for most passengers. Seat reclines. Aisle requires people to walk sideways to navigate. Insufficient storage, many bags had to be checked at gate.

Was sat in the emergency exit row. Ample leg room but was a little tight with elbow room. Entertainment system was ok but would prefer a newer movie selection. Breakfast meal was a little heavy, but enjoyed the selection including fruit, yogurt and croissant. Service professional and courteous. Overall the flight was enjoyable
Attention it's a plus. They spoil me all the flight. Food was great also wines. The desserts was the best. Full lie flat bed, loved it! The lounge at Paris was just OK. Could be better.

Never again. The seats are incredibly close together. In case of an emergency, I doubt many people could get out in an efficient manner. There are seats with more leg room but you have to pay a premium for that. The seats are hard and uncomfortable. They also do not recline. This makes sense because you would recline into the person's face behind you. On top of that, the Flair App kept crashing so no in-flight entertainment. I know this is a discount airline but the experience was worse than bottom basement pricing. The flight had only 29 passengers with capacity for 186. When I asked to move to a seat with more leg room I was denied since I did not pay for that. 30 minutes into the flight I moved anyway and got dirty looks from the flight attendant. She did not approach me though, maybe because she realised how ridiculous it was to deny me.

My flight was from Mumbai to Bahrain and then Bahrain to Istanbul. The flight from Mumbai to Bahrain was good with good seats and reclining. Bahrain to Istanbul was a normal seat (one cannot sleep) but that depends on the aircraft chosen (I understand) but the reclining option was not working. So I was on a Business Class Seat, late in the Night and the seat was not reclining. It was super uncomfortable and the Staff said 'Sorry" as nothing could be done and other seats were full.

The seat is uncomfortable and the tray table is unusable if you neighbor in front reclines his seat.  Usage of infotainment system is also difficult, since reclined seat in front, will bring the screen very close to your face.

Overall Cathay Pacific economy class seat is not top in the class but overall it's fine. Their seats have similar comfort than the competitors. Legroom is alright but I won't say it's top notch. Cathay Pacific offers pillow and blanket for each seat. I managed to have a decent 2 hour sleep. Cathay Pacific could certainly do better on the comfort of economy class seats.

Seat quality is fairly average. The seats are not comfy but acceptable for short haul flight. No entertainment screen so I watched movies from my iPad. There's USB ports where you can charge your devices and gadgets.

Newer plane. Great seat arrangement 1-2-1. We had the middle seats. Seats were comfortable, lots of storage and plenty of space to work with and store in. Although no sliding doors for privacy, but the seats are situated in a way that not much is visible by the seat across the isle and vice versa. I will definitely recommend the KLM's 787 business class.

Brilliant service and facilities. The QSuites product is best in class and has set a very high bar. Food and beverage excellent, quality top notch. Al Mourjan lounge definitely one of best business class lounges in the world.
Never again, hardly any legroom, seats were worn out, uncomfortable and almost no cushioning left. Hardly any storage in the seat pocket as they store lots of pointless magazines etc in there

Extremely short legroom, very uncomfortable chairs, even with a higher rate what you get is just the chair reclines, not suitable for tall people or long flights. Alsoo in two different trips the flight had delays in departure, the first one of an hour and the next flight more than 3 hours

The worst service and horrific baggage handling practices! This was a round trip. It started well on the way to our holiday with a relatively good service. It all changed on the flight home to Melbourne. Shortly after locating my seat, I discovered that it was wet smelling like urine. It took my fellow passenger going directly to one of the staff for them to actually address my wet seat and replace it. This is the airline I will definitely avoid at all cost!

Seats are broken, they squeak when you relax and annoying. Imagine sleeping in an environment where snoring, squeaking continuously going on and flight duration is 14 hours or so. Dirt is all around with broken or non functional TV monitors, remote wire pulled stuck and doesn’t retract. Seats are not comfortable for heavy person like me. Call for attendant it stays lit and No one bothers to show up.

I flew from LAX to Zurich and back to LAX with Swiss airlines. On both flights the seats were so narrow that when I saw my middle seat on the outbound flight I was thinking whether I'll fit in that space. And I'm not a big guy by any means (5':10" = 178cm tall, 155lb=70Kg). On the return flight I paid 44Euros and got an isle seat but when I boarded I saw an overweight lady sitting in the adjacent seat and the arm-rest was not coming down! Thanks got her husband was elsewhere and we changed seats. The overhead luggage space is so narrow that you should put your carry-on sideways. Their planes are not really suitable for long distances.  As for the on-flight entertainment system, It was showing advertisements and you where not given option to watch a movie or something until one hour into flight. Their food and beverage service was OK like any other reasonable airline.

On long haul flight Istanbul-Jakarta (and back) seats were quite narrow. I saw seat features map with 3x3x3 layout in the last aircraft compartment, in reality the middle section has four seats, so 3x4x3. Pitch is not good either, and not suitable for long haul flight. Everything felt squashed. The recline was okay-ish. The seat padding felt comfortable though, but this is not enough to make up for shortcomings re the seat width and pitch.

Visibly uncleaned and undisinfected lounge after the previous flight! Old, almost worn out and visibly not regularly cleaned upholstery on the seats. Narrow and uncomfortable. Видимо непочистен и недезинфекциран салон след предишния полет. Стара, почти захабена и видимо непочиствана редовно тапицерия на седалките! Тесни и неудобни.

I recently flew with Garuda Indonesia from Jakarta to Shanghai, and it was a very disappointing experience. The seat was extremely uncomfortable, making the long flight unbearable. To make matters worse, the seat was dirty and had an unpleasant smell. The seat was too straight, preventing my neck from relaxing.  I noticed other passengers complaining about the same issues, and everyone kept adjusting their body positions to try and feel better. I expected much better service and will think twice before flying with Garuda Indonesia again.

We flew transatlantic from London (LGW) in October 2024. Upgraded to econoflex seats thinking it would be similar to economy plus on Air Canada with more space in the seat. The seats we got were no better than all the other economy seats and they were the most cramped and uncomfortable seats I have ever experienced; minimal padding and very narrow. So tight was the legroom, I could not physically reach down to the floor to retrieve items I dropped - i am not a large person at 5’ 7” and 160lbs. We booked three seats for three people but found there was no window in our row (9) on the left (port) side of the aircraft. It was not possible to read a magazine horizontally in front of me, it was propped up by the seat back in front of me. The seat pockets are fitted with inflexible netting which does not allow much to be stored; I had trouble getting my water bottle into the net. There are no screens in the rear of the seats; passengers must use their own devices to access the entertainment system which was not as extensive as other airlines provide. It was rudimentary and holding a phone or iPad up for the duration of the flight was a chore. The flight information was also pretty basic. WestJet have opted for only two toilets at each end of the aircraft, one for the economy cabin and another for business class. Not nearly enough for the number of passengers aboard since economy pax are asked not to use the business class bathrooms when the tiny curtain is across the aisle. I feel sorry for the cabin crew who have to work in extremely tight spaces. I think there was more space in the overhead bins than was provided for passengers. Finally, the overhead air nozzles were pathetic and provided a weak airstream despite our best efforts to adjust them while at the same time the aircraft interior was too warm for the entire flight.

My business class seat 3D was broken and would not move. The staff took off the cushions and laid it flat with a manual handle where it stayed for the remainder of the 11hr flight AKL to SCL. When I contacted LATAM Customer Support they declined to offer any sort of recompense at all because an official report wasn't made by the staff, after she told me that she would.

The seat is bolt upright, with no adjustment or storage. While a seat like this might be suitable for ultra short haul it is not suitable for a flight of four hours. Very uncomfortable seat, it must be the worst in class. It deserves a zero rating.

Premium economy from Boston to Munich. Seat had good legroom, much better than economy at close to double the price. My main seat complaint is the fixed arm rest. My wife and I take 2 seats on the side on purpose but this strategy provides less room when the center arm rests are fixed. Entertainment system was good. I didn’t eat but food seemed economy-average. One point - the menu listed Warsteiner beer (a great beer) but they actually only had a skunked Beck;s (not a great beer). Also there was no amenity kit provided despite this being advertised. Overall a good, not great experience, potentially worth it for a 6’ tall passenger who can afford it. Not as good as some others.

Normally with Allegiant we pay the upcharge for the extra legroom seats, but due to a recent Covid exposure we had to modify our travel dates and there were no extra legroom seats available. So we got stuck in standard seats, my wife in a window seat and me in an aisle. My wife is 6 feet tall with a 32 inch inseam, and I'm 6 foot 2 with a 30 inch inseam. The legroom was miserable. I can't imagine anyone with an even longer leg length shoe-horning into these seats. Hard to believe the FAA permits such small spacing, or that people will loyally fly in such seats. In future I shall only book extra legroom seats with Allegiant - or will fly other airlines. Otherwise I have no problem with Allegiant's business model and approach. But this is a showstopper for us.
Seats are extremely uncomfortable, too hard and it’s impossible to be in one position over an hour, which makes it impossible to sleep. Not a good option for an overnight flight.

Seat layout was quite good in that there appears more knee room than other airlines with similar aircraft. The seats themselves, I thought were terrible. Little shape and a headrest that is too far from your head. So I could not lean back to rest my head without straining my neck. Perhaps all that model of aircraft are like that? I will take more notice on future flights.

The seats are alright, about the same as other airlines, head rest and shoulder rest comfort are acceptable but nothing surprising. The entertainment was great with one USB charging port available. There is 2 aisles in economy class cabin on the A330.

The 3x3x3 configuration on the A350-900 is desperately cramped. I have short legs but my knees were knocking against the seat in front and the 6 flights comprising my journey from London to Perth and return were spent with a neighbour's elbow poking into my side because of the narrowness of the seat and the armrest. Hard seats compounded the problem. No refresher towels or overnight comfort packs except a skimpy one on the outward leg on SA. Minimal food choice, and what was provided to me was inedible apart.

Got to my seat, width was lovely, Leg room was great, reclining seat marvellous. After 15 minutes it was the worst comfort i have ever had in a seat ever, long haul or short haul. Felt like I was sitting on a plank of wood for every journey i made.  Everything else was great, please put another review for overall comfort as these seats are terrible.
Seat was the worst that I've seen on a long flight. Hard and uncomfortable seats that recline poorly and terrible legroom. The seat caused me back pain for a long time.

I flew the lie flat seat from Narita to LAX on their Boeing 787. The check in was fast. I had prepaid for the checked in luggage as well as the meals on board. The lie flat seat was very comfortable. In fact, it was more comfortable than some business class lie flat seats. The free WiFi on board was virtually non existent. But that was ok since i downloaded some movies from Netflix prior to boarding. The plane was clean and modern. No complaints there. I was able to order water and snacks from my iphone. The prices were reasonable for snacks, meals and beverages. For lie flat seats, this was a bargain. The airfare was almost one third the cost of flying business class on other airlines. It was a very good value for the money. I would definitely fly Zip Air again to go to Japan.

I opted for a regular economy seat on the Mumbai-Doha leg of the flight and a preferred seat on the Doha-Chicago leg. Unfortunately the seats were disappointing and uncomfortable. Lumbar support was poor, my leg space was compromised with IFE boxes intruding into he foot well which made the Doha -Chicago leg really uncomfortable. There were only USB charging points on the seat.

This review is for Warsaw to Chicago, Sept 5, 2023. Also, this is our first, and most likely last time we will fly on LOT. Positives: Very attentive and kind cabin crew. Plenty of beverages throughout the flight. Meals were somewhat basic (dinner and 'breakfast'), but adequate. Negatives: Very, very cramped. Not much space between rows, and even less when person in front of you reclines their seat. Given how little room there is, it is understandable that someone may want more space, but then there is no room to use your seat table. My wife had a drink on hers, which spilled when the person in front of her reclined their seat. If you drop something, good luck trying to find it while inflight. Aisles very narrow, barely any room to walk. For a 10+ hour flight, this is not a good choice.
One of the most comfortable seats with more than average knee room in economy class. I have travelled economy in varying airlines and I found this to be the best.

Got in the seat, everything was fine first 30 mins then felt like I was sitting on solid concrete or even wood, lower back so painful I couldn't move until I landed in Dubai second flight wasn't as bad as there was no one sitting next to me had a little more room, still couldnt move. The main problem was the meals, Nearly less than a year before I travelled (I can't remember exactly Dec 22-Feb 23) I contacted There call centre that I have food allergies (wholemeal items, mushroom, fish) and I already knew especially second flight those items were on the menu. The online help agent said bring your own meals, I made him aware they will be taken off me at departing airport, he said they wouldnt, they were taken off me. Then advised take the bland meal option you'll be fine, first option had mushroom, second meal had fish. I felt unwell for a hour or so onboard, The crew was surprised when I hand the whole meal back untouched when they collected rubbish. I go every year to Japan, the time on emirates are great as the return gives me virtually the full last day, others I lose it, for 2024 or 2025 I will be using another airline. The "help" desk is terrible. I've been in so called airlines considered not as good customer service who have been great. I know my return back to Dubai I have the same problem awaiting help desk said there is nothing they can do, not there problem.

Surprisingly good seat next to the window, 64A. 2 windows at this seat. USB charger as well as option for charging with a plug. Felt the personal entertainment screen was a good size. Watched 6 movies on the 16 hour flight. Since the flight was not full, economy passengers were spaced around the cabin mostly with a seat between them.

Most uncomfortable seat I have ever been in, especially since it was a 5 hour flight. Absolutely no leg room, poor recline on seats, hard uncomfortable, narrow seats. The pilot and staff did a great job but this is a review of the plane not the staff.

Gate crew at JFK Terminal 7 Alaska Airlines were of such a degree of incompetence despite ; would not allow us to take on one carry on + one personal item each because of the excuse "no room". After we got on the aircraft, it turns out there was loads of room - they are simply bad at counting. Then told us we still weren't allowed to take the luggage on because the "bag had already been tagged". Aircraft itself has no screen for entertainment even in business class. You have to bring your own laptop to pass the time to the 6 hour flight. Business class gets food; all other classes get nothing.

I was seated in exit row in the economy class cabin. The seat was perhaps the worst I have ever had the privilege of using. The seat was torn, dirty and shabby with absolutely no storage space of any kind. The head rest had lost its shape and the cushioning was worn out, the tray table barely holding together and the backrest was in a weird angle which made it impossible to find a comfortable seating position. The best part was that the IFE remote is big and bulges into the seat making the narrow seat even more painful since it digs painfully into your hip all the time and just because you have a remote doesn't mean that it works since IFE was not operating on almost all seats of the aircraft due to the ancient monitors which must have been broken. The 15 hour journey on this seat from Delhi to Chicago was an epic nightmare. The only good part was the ample legroom since this seat was right next to the lavatory.

First class seat in the aisle out of the galley and aircraft entrance that sits too close to the bulkhead to stretch legs. During boarding people keep bumping on you and you have to watch your legs every time flight attendants come in and out of the galley. Worst seat of the entire 1st class cabin. Recline is OK for regional 1st class service.

Headrest is fixed and not changeable. Armrest are 2 small foldable tables.  IFE Flightinfo can not save changes to metric system by each change to movie or music an return to flight info. Touchbuttons to change the seat not working (crew needs to change the seat to bed). Bed is not to sleep for passengers who sleep on sides. Hole for feet is to small for footsize 46.

Absolutely do not sit in row 15 (directly in front of exit row). The seats will not recline, but the row in front of you does, so you're left with maybe 12 inches between your face and the seat in front of you. Also the seat is so upright it feels like it's trying to push you out. I've flown on a few United flights for this business trip and I am not impressed with the seat comfort, layout, or timeliness of the airline in general. Of the 7 flights this week, all but 1 has been late departure/arrival.

Seats are so uncomfortable, you have a very little legroom space, seats do not recline and one of the planes I travelled did not have USB port. In a 6 hour flight, New York to Bogota, the plane did not have screens but did have a website for entertainment but it’s not the same. They did not offer a glass of water for free, you had to pay for everything. Do not fly with Avianca on international flights, it’s so uncomfortable.

I flew Toronto to Delhi on Jan 19, 2023 and Returned on Feb 15, 2023. On both the flights my seat was changed at the time of Boarding. Seat deficiency was sited as a reason. The seats assigned to me on January 19 was 14A . This seat did not work as it could not be straightened and I got the worst hip pain at this seat. The hostess offered me another seat, which could not be reclined and had to change from one to the other. Very uncomfortable. The seat assigned to me on Feb 15 was 12A. This seat minimally straightened and reclined. The TV remote was stuck. could not use it even after cold boot of the system. Having spent a significant amount of money for this travel, the comfort was missing on both the flights and my major concern was my hip getting strained.

Currently sitting on my flight from Colombo to Dubai and I'm shocked at how uncomfortable the economy class seats are. The middle of the seat has a big metal lump protruding out of it and when you lift the headrest, your shoulders are resting on more hard metal. The actual shape of the seats are awful too. They're almost curved so you feel like you're sitting like this: C. Not to mention the seats are thread bare with little to no cushion on them. The only thing I'm grateful for is the fact my flight is only 4.5hrs long, I don't know how I'd be able to cope with any longer. If you're considering Sri Lankan for a long-haul flight in economy and comfort is important for you, I'd strongly suggest you look elsewhere.

Worst business class seat I have experienced Automatic seat controls did not work on either the outbound or return flight, so flight attendant assistance was required several times. Same with the center wall divider partition that required attendant assistance to lock it in place for both flights. Seat design requires you to lie at an angle in order to use the foot rest space. Overall, was not impressed with this business class product &amp.

More than I expected. Flights were on time, service was good, you get what you paid for, fares are very reasonable, and love having a direct flight from point A to point B. Only caution though is on the legroom - row 5 A/B/C very light compared to the other side of the row 5 D/E/F.

My issues are the seats are too hard for the 4+ hour flight to Gran Canaria (general feeling amongst all those whose backside was numb by the time the plane landed). They won't pay for a terminal link but coach everyone out to the plane, this means the flights are always late taking off.

Seat 4A on Flair’s Boeing 737-800 is good. You get 2 windows and a nice view of the engine, but 5A is better for that view. When I flew the 4A, B, and C row was empty except for me. Seat felt kind of hard though. On my flight it had a charging outlet, but didn’t work

Chose a window seat so I could lean against the pillow and window as I usually do. But due to large gap between seat and arm ready window side it was very uncomfortable. Leg room minimal. I’m 5,5 . It seems new but not well designed. Tray table not adjustable and too close to body.

Very bad service, the food was awful, the drink options were not good. No champagne for a business class. The seat is a joke, very tight and uncomfortable, even though it was one of the newest aircraft from the market. The checkin was the worst, I got a boarding pass that did not work, I couldn’t even get the digital one and no airport staff printed me a new one even I explained that was not working they haven’t reprinted it for me.

This was by far the most uncomfortable flight. Seats are incredibly hard and way too narrow for any comfort. I had booked an aisle and my boyfriend had the window seat. Most of the time, nobody will take the middle, unless the flight is at capacity. Unfortunately, this time I was asked to move into the middle seat and was sandwiched between two very large men whose shoulders far exceeded the width of the seat, including my own. I am also not a tiny person. I had to sit wedged sideways just to fit and dislocated a rib in the process. I used to enjoy flying with Air Transat, but this has gotten way out of hand. It is truly appalling and cruel to treat people this way. There are only 12 club class on this airline so 12 people can pay an exorbitant amount to be comfortable while the other 300+ passengers get to travel in extreme discomfort.

Seats are better than what would be expected of a 42 seater aircraft. sufficient legroom, width and recline. nice, clean and soft. my seat was positioned and aligned with the window for a perfect view of mountains and terrains we were flying over and beside. 5A was where I was seating on. sufficient space in the overhead cabin. Overall very good.

The flight from Frankfurt to Oslo is only about 2 hours long and we of course know that seats have limited comfort and space. However, these seats and the space offered were considerably below our expectations. The seats are hard but the problem is the space which is very limited and feel cramped. Working with a laptop or eating is virtually impossible for a grown man who can only pray that the person in front is not recline their seat. It can be that the official figures show enough space but for all of us (we were 5 in the group), it was cramped and uncomfortable.

This 17 inch seat and a 31" pitch for an international flight was horrible. I sat near the window and paid extra to pick the seat. I was in seat 18 at the window both to and from San Diego to Germany. If the seat number 16 in front of me had their seat back, I could not move. The passengers at the end of my 3 seat row, had extra leg room, but the carts kept running into them. If there was an emergency, I would have been stuck, because the seats are so close to the seats in front of them you cannot move past the other passengers in the row. The seats seam to be made of a polyester material that is slippery. When I would put my seat back and my legs reclined, I would slip down the seat. There was not way to sleep or be comfortable. If you fly an airline, whose economy seats are so small, it will be one of the worst flights of your life. Next time I will check the size of the seats.

I travelled on 4 international flights with this airline on a recent trip. 3 were satisfactory. The 4th was a nightmare. The aisle widths and the seats have been reduced to accommodate more passengers. The seats are sublimely uncomfortable with pain in any position after about 15 minutes. I sat on the aisle and a large man sat in the middle who simply did not fit in the seat and encroached into my seat. I could choose to sit in contact with him from shoulder to knee or stick out in the aisle and be jostled by every passerby. It was a nightmarish flight overnight from Nairobi to Amsterdam. KLM obviously has no regard for its passengers to subject them to such torture and I will make every effort to avoid this airline in future.

Wasn’t impressed with this flight at all - no air vents above the seat, and cabin temperature fluctuated between 23/25 degrees throughout the whole flight on both legs from LHR - SYD. The purser wouldn’t adjust the cabin temperature as she stated that other passengers were cold, so had to provide me with a fan. Seat was really uncomfortable as a bed, and didn’t find the basic adjustments to the seat formation comfortable at all. Meal options were ok but very rigid - if you didn’t like an aspect of your menu selection, there were no alternatives. Staff were friendly and tried their best to be helpful.
The seats were hard and didn't recline. Very uncomfortable. It gave me a terrible back pain. It is amazing how airlines try to maximize profit at the expense of comfort and health.

Horrible experience, I have paid for the extra leg room seat and the seats in aircraft was disgusting and very uncomfortable. It was not pushing back or once it's pushed back it was not staying still. In 4 of the booked seats, 3 of the seats with broken entertainment screens. Travelled multiple times with multiple airlines but this was an worse experience. Compare to any other airlines cost of tickets was nearly similar.

During our return trip from Tokyo to Frankfurt we were assigned a seat in the lower deck of the business class section, which was broken, making the 11-hour and 40-minute flight extremely uncomfortable. When we brought this to the attention of the head flight attendant, she was apologetic, but did not offer any solution other than the manual manipulation of the seat, every time we needed to change its position. To our surprise, we found two members of what we believe was an orchestra seated in the upper deck of the business class section with their cellos strapped into chairs next to them. We feel that the head flight attendant could have easily asked one of them to switch seats with us, as the cellos would not have minded if their seat did not recline. Instead, we had to manually manipulate the seat every time we needed to change positions. Although the flight attendants offered to compensate us for the damaged seat, they changed their minds three times, stating that the compensation was only offered to European travelers, not Americans. Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the level of customer service on this flight, and afterward. For the high price of a business class ticket, I expected much better treatment and a more comfortable experience.

Not really comfortable chair or bed. Singapore Airlines offer a proper bed and a separate chair in First Suite: Both are rather disappointing, especially taken into account the huge investment and Publicity. The leather chair stands alone in the middle of the Suite, one has to move it from the take-off position, to the dining position, and to the outside view position. The bed is not facing the direction of travel, but crossways in the suite. The bed is narrow and very hard, not very comfortable. When the bed is not used, it hangs across the suite like a chunk of white painted wood. The whole design is not well thought through and not nicely done.

I didn't expect much from a low-fare flight but the seats were bad even in those standards. We're talking about stiff seats, where one can feel the plywood underneath one's behind. No reclining, no neck support, and nothing but the bare necessities to allow you to strap yourself in and pray for the flight to end.

I hate to say it but this would have to be the worst Business Class offering I have flown in over 20years. The seats we were allocated in row 2, and were barley even a decent premium economy seat. They were tight uncomfortable and cramped. My wife who had the window seat said it felt like she was trapped in a box. The amount of space allocated for these two seats is appalling. There was no storage whatsoever, not even to rest a drink bottle. Never again.

We flew TK62 from IST to KUL in seats 3E/3F. Upon arrival, we saw industrial tapes on the middle divider between the seats. The tapes hardly hold the divider down and we in the end have to use a blanket in the middle slot to keep it down throughout the flight. No crew acknowledgement or apologies for such inconvenience.

Avoid Seat 1J on the A350. The only window is non operational with the blind locked closed for whatever reason. As an older traveler who likes to look out of the window in order to focus my eyesight, this was terrible. Considering the cost of this ticket (and very poor crew service today), we shall be changing our future AF flights.
Horrible seats. Very narrow you can barely fit into it, and the leg room was awful. The headrests couldn't be moved, and the seat kept reclining because it wasn't working. Very uncomfortable.
Good seats, a little better than average, very good tv. The tv has a lot of options, exterior camera view, very good map. Nice quality and good chargers.

Pretty standard business class offering with just 3 rows in business. Rock hard seat with middle seat kept free. Reasonable leg room. The flight is short but I wouldn't want this seat if flying for much longer. The plane - OE-LZO is only 5 weeks old so it is still spangly and new. USB A&C for each seat. The flight was a 6am LHR-VIE so breakfast was served. I didn't much like the blueberry cake thing, but the meat/cheese/tomato combo was decent. Croissants and rolls were offered. Excellent coffee. Overall, not bad but could be better.
Very uncomfortable seats. Very narrow. No information about the flight on the seat’s screen, only the remaining time until arrival. No free headsets to watch the only 10 films they have available.

I have never been so uncomfortable for 11hrs. I'm 6ft tall and had almost no legroom. When the chair in front of me was reclined I had even less legroom and the joy of another chair basically in my lap which also made it very difficult to watch my low quality screen. This was flat out painful and I really don't recommend this for anyone.

We were fortunate enough to get the extra legroom seats but were not able to sit together because the staff on Etihad phone service refused to link our bookings, which were booked separately. Their entire raison detre is to get you off the phone with no action on their part. The cabin crew and ground staff were great. Food was so so. The main beef is a full service airline should not be charging for standard seat selection. On that basis we will never fly Etihad again.

These seats are the worst. First off they're stained and filthy, they are barely wide enough for an average adult, my waste is 34 and I was very uncomfortable. I had paid for bulkhead row as I knew the legroom was tight, and even there I wasn't comfortable at all. $60 for extra legroom and I couldn't even cross my legs because I'd be within the wall, the seats are too close to the walls of the cabin, and they don't recline so you're very uncomfortable the entire flight.

Rows 12 and 13 - emergency exit, more space. Slim chairs, not reclining, more comfort due to large space between the rows. Extra payment is needed (€ 20-40, depending on flight) or frequent flyer pass (€ 249 year, with other benefits included - priority boarding and large cabin bag).

I like to check seat maps and reviews before booking my flights. In case of my Toronto to Lisbon flight with TAP Portugal, I was unable to find any seat reviews online for this aircraft. I paid a significant premium to select 12F, an exit row window seat. This was an overnight flight, so I thought this would be a good opportunity to sleep. Unfortunately, the seat was extremely narrow, hard, width-restricted by those fixed armrests that you typically only see at bulkhead seats and also missing an armrest on the fuselage side. Also, it was surprising that the person in 11F was able to recline their seat. Exit Rows are not supposed to be able to be reclined into. There was also a very cold draft coming from the fuselage. The seat was so uncomfortable, that I spent the last 2 hours of the flight sitting on the floor and using my winter jacket to cover myself. Granted this was only possible because I had the exit-row legroom. In summary, selecting an exit row window seat on a a Tap Portugal A321Neo-LR is not wise and it is definitely not worth the premium price-tag they place on it.

Nice looking seat with adequate storage and large video screen. Unfortunately seat felt hard / uncomfortable after a few hours. Inflight bedding was soft and plush, but when the seat transformed into bed it still was not enough to help soften bed. Simply could not get comfortable. I really wanted to like this seat as its aesthetics were really nice. Definitely an improvement over the older Delta One, but the seats could benefit from a bit more cushioning.

The most uncomfortable flight I have experienced due to the metal boxes under the seat in front. Outbound chose a window seat on lower deck and had one metal box under my seat that made sitting straight very difficult, so on way home opted for an upper deck seat in a set of two with my husband so I could at least get up and stretch. There was two boxes this time, and had pins and needles in my legs for not only the entire flight but for several hours afterwards. As vegan flyers we are never wowed with food, but this one was the worst yet, plain rice and vegetables.

One of the worst flights I have taken in recent years, I have flown Lufthansa before, and it was not like this before. The seats were so congested, the TV screen was too small and did not work, touch screen will not respond, extremely poor audio even with high quality headset. Food on our way was Ok, quality needs improvement, food service from Frankfort to Jordan was the worst, clod cheese sandwich. The flight from Cairo to Frankfurt, seats will not recline and so hard, sitting in those seats gives backpain. Frankfort to Houston, same A330, worst seating, recline won’t work, someone had to push up/down for recline to work, window seat is the worst, half of your leg space is taken by some aircraft equipment box.

The seats were absolutely terrible in every way. Felt like sitting on concrete. The cushions were poorly attached and slid around when you moved. There was little to no back support. No legroom whatsoever. I literally could not sit with my legs in front of me, and could barely fit my backpack under the seat. Also no power outlet anywhere.

Zero comfort, unfit to anyone taller than 1.60m, old fashion 1980's bulky seats, does not recline, in immediate contact to the wall behind. Unbelievably ITA charges premium fares and delivers less than low cost airlines quality.
The 777 are awful to fly in. Ridiculous, narrow seats and limited legroom. In comparison to the A380, with wide seats and better legroom. Seats a bit hard after 15 hours.

Flew economy comfort, horrible seat, after six hours you do not know anymore to sit comfortable. After 10 hours you are completely broken and your back really hurts. No more cushion is provided by KLM in economy (comfort) class. This cushion could provide you with some support in lower back.

Service was excellent. Food and beverage were also according to market level. The main problem here are the seats. It took Lufthansa forever to initiate the transition to newer business class seats. Despite the announcement of their new business class seats, who knows when we can finally experience it. Current seats do not match Lufthansa's pricing that skyrocketed and is I would say one of the worst in the premium segment. This is only compensated by the nice mileage program, service and staff.

Do you relish the thought of the seat in front of you being mere inches from your face when you take an international flight? How about dreaming of your backside numb for hours on end because there is no viable escape if you are in a window seat? What are your thoughts on a cabin temperature kept to a steady 80 degrees? If these things, and experiences just like them, are your idea of a good time, forge ahead. I’ve been to Iceland around 40 times since 2012. I tolerated the increasingly ancient 757s interiors because I knew the Max 8 was coming. It seems like a lost opportunity. The seating experience is just so bad that any attempt to overcome via in flight service and amenities is lost. One less row in this plane and you can be a human. I fly all manner of classes for work all over the world. Often I get the great lie flat business class seats because I am a United 1k member but I also often am in economy, and that’s OK. It evens out. But this is just ridiculous.
Worst seat we have ever had to endure on a long haul flight. No room at all and not what we expected would not recommend this airline

The seats are clean. They can be reclined a few degrees. Seat width is standard and ok for a normal sized person. The distance to the front seat is just long enough to not touch it although one has to sit completely straight. For a budget airline, the cabin feels rather roomy and doesn’t make one feel claustrophobic like in other airlines.

United has audacity to call their product "First Class". I tried to sit in seat 4E on my flight yesterday from ABQ-SFO. The seats were old and dingy looking. The lumbar support was sticking out into my back like a rock. The button to control it was broken. I basically had to lean forward the entire flight. I will do my best to never fly United again. A truly garbage seat from an airline that obviously doesn't care.

During this flight, there was a child seated directly in front of me who attempted to throw things at myself and my seat mates, kept touching my screen, would not stay seated and parents would not control him. When I alerted the stewardess  she said "give it a minute". His behavior continued on and off about ever 20-30 minutes during this 14+ hour flight. I asked to be moved to another seat. At first, I was informed that the flight was fully booked. The 3rd time I asked to be moved, she moved me to one open seat which happened to be by the bathroom. So I was moved from one noisy, loud, and overly active and disruptive child to a seat where I could now smell the toilets, which created nausea. When I was returning to the original seat by the overly active and disruptive child, she said "Are you having one of those days? I'm sorry but there's nothing I can do for you?" It wasn't that there was nothing she could do, it was that she chose to do the very least and that was nothing. There was open seating in business class and she did not offer which is ridiculous customer service. This child was throwing things, the parents refused to control the child. They let the child sleep on the floor several times when another stewardess informed them that the child could not sleep on the floor. She could not control the parents of the child nor the child and refused to assist me to have a peaceful experience on the 14+ hour flight I paid for. It's as if my investment in the ticket was not as good as theirs. When I pressed the button for a stewardess she was no where to be found as the flight went on. I had an amazing flight going to Dubai, the staff of flight EK0236 was very friendly but this one stewardess for flight EK0235 ruined my entire experience by not rectifying the situation with the child and the parents. Who wants to sit in a plane for 14hr having thing thrown at them or the child touching their screen while they are trying to watch a movie? It was unbearable and unbelievable.

I miss the old AA economy seats with IFE. The new seats introduced a few years ago stripped out the IFE and some seat padding. The new seats do offer more storage though. The WI-FI on board still is okay but not the best. The seats are survivable for 4 hours and the device holder is handy. Legroom remains the same and the seat width is better than the 737. The A320 family fleet of American Airlines is usually more comfortable than their Boeing aircraft. I do prefer the older seats with IFE though.

Worst aircraft. The seat didn’t recline as the button didn’t seem to work. The inflight screen didn’t work as the touchscreen plus the controls were broken. We spent 8 hours of the flight staring at the air India logo on the screen. USB broken so couldn’t charge our phones either. Never flying Air India again.

Seats are too small for a 6 hours service. This was the worst seat experience I have had. Normally, they can use seats like this for a 1 hour flight, but it's very shocking to use this configuration for a long journey. No seat recline, no individual tv set for a 6 hour flight. No power socket to charge phone for a 6 hour flight.

Genuinely awful! Like flying cross-country in a lawn chair. I’m only slightly above average height and I had to wedge my legs into place with my arms. Seats don’t recline, don’t have power sources, and don’t have TVs.

This is a QSuite seat. The seat is very roomy and ergonomically arranged. Storage is sufficient and the sliding door gives enough privacy. If one travels with a partner, the middle divider can be lowered, making this a private 2-person Suite. The seat is very well suited for a long night on a plane. One of the best seats I’ve travelled in.

Better that expected. After reading some of these reviews we were a little concerned. My wife and mother-in-law travelled Saskatoon to Vancouver. We decided to give Flair a try due to the very high rates from Air Canada and Westjet. The booking was very easy. If you travel with just a carry-on it is very cheap. Checking bags is where they recover their discounted rates. ~$75/bag. Expensive but still significantly cheaper than AC and WJ. The booking was easy. Regular reminders can on our phones and email. Check-in on-line was very easy. The plane left on time and arrived on time. The staff at the gate were very helpful and courteous. My wife noted how helpful Betty was. She was an air hostess on the plane. The plane was smooth on take off and landing. Overall a good experience. We will fly Flair again. At least we have another choice. When people write a review they should write it based on a "Discount" airline.

Boeing 787-9 - not worth the money. The seats were extremely narrow so like lying in a coffin. When the seats were out (which is all the time on these long flights) you have to clamber over passengers to get to the toilet. The configuration of the cabin means that some one is always waking up someone else. This is an economy seat masquerading as a business class seat and is misleading and deceptive conduct because there is NO WAY you can get any rest if you book with British Airways.
Seat 26A. This was a randomly allocated seat, and in terms of the view, behind the wing on the port side (left) of the plane. Good view and good legroom for the price paid.

The aircraft was clean and tidy - inflight entertainment was very good, seating with 3x4x3 layout. The staff were nice but having asked to give a glass of water before takeoff, the staff didnt bother and totally forgotten.

Took SilkAir again from SIN-SUB and SUB-SIN on MI225/226. The new WIFI Inflight entertainment was very nice and there is a booklet to tell us how to connect and it is helpful - although you may be confused for first time user. They also played shows on the overhead screens (without sounds though). Seat was comfortable and with good recline and plenty of legroom for tall people.

Buenos Aires to Paris return on Boeing 777. Seats narrow, the front seat almost on my face. Impossible to rest neither sleep. I'm 1,83m and wieght 84kgs. normal size. It so small the tray that it makes impossible to eat and the tray where they bring the meal is so tiny you can't eat.

Rock hard seat cushion, unwatchable TV screen and IFE box taking up half of your foot space, really let Swiss long haul down. On the plus side, food and drinks were very good and plentiful, cabin crew on the whole friendly and efficient. Not going to complain about seat width and pitch as this information is easily found out beforehand and therefore can't come as a surprise - needless to say most airlines have roughly the same seat pitch/width, so it's the food and entertainment system that gets votes. We all wish that we had a bit more room in economy but that's not what lets Swiss down in my opinion.

Boarding from Gatwick was smooth and quick, even after an hour delay. First impression of the cabin was oaky, the tray tables were dirty but that wasn't an issue. The seats do not recline which is good. We had lots of legroom due to the shape of the seats. Cabin crew were great and flight time was good.

I flew for the first time with Qatar Airways, JFK-DOH-LHE. The check-in process was very fast because I checked in online. Food was great, and cabin staff was very helpful. Even though my return flight was delayed 2hrs from Lahore due to mechanical issue, when we arrived at DOH ground staff expedited us to JFK flight. Overall, a great experience with Qatar Airways.

I had not heard of the airline, and looked up Qatar Airways on Skytrax and was surprised to find a lot of positive reviews and a quick Google search gave me a lot of confidence. The flight itself was 2 international trips, Melbourne to Athens through Doha, and Madrid to Melbourne through Doha. The long legs between Melbourne and Doha were on the Boeing 777s in their 3x3x3 layout. Staff were extremely helpful and very accommodating, and a lot of diversity as well. Seats were spacious and comfortable and I never really felt uncomfortable or cramped. Food was pretty good and was delighted to be served several meals in my flight, with access to as much water, soda and snacks as I desired. In general, the staff were great, the planes were clean and tidy, the experience was top notch and I was extremely happy to fly with them. Best of all the flying was top notch without a single incident. Economy class took on a whole new meaning with Qatar and I'll fly with them again soon.

Seating felt like being squeezed in from side. Distance from other seat I think the worst I have seen. I thought Etihad being from UAE will be at par or better than Emirates - they proved me wrong. So far off from Emirates in everything that I am surprised that they are from same place. Anyway, one time was enough for me.

Buenos Aires - Rome on Boeing 777 with Alitalia premium economy. Seats uncomfortable very difficult resting and sleeping. No entertainment system working on the plane! Food was an economy product. If the difference with economy in money is big I wouldn't pay. There is not to much space than economy with the front seat. As it is a shell seat it slides it does not recline and it is very hard it does not have padding or it have been used so much it worn out.

Not impressed with Japan Airlines Premium Economy seat. Looks fancy with hard shell and forward slide. Fancy concepts don't translate to comfort in real life. Couldn't find a comfortable position. Not much slide to speak of. Despite sleeping pills, couldn't get comfortable enough to sleep.

Asiana is a pretty good airline. The seats were comfortable enough as airplane seats in general. The food on the flight was mainly Korean, so if you are not accustomed to Korean or Asian food, it may be a shock. The service was really good and the flight attendants were all really sweet.

Seat 6C, Boeing 787 Dreamliner. Scoot advertises this seat as having additional legroom, this is not the case. At this time I would not recommend that anybody does a seat upgrade on this airline. As far as I am concerned, the seats are getting smaller and smaller, with less and less padding. It's even difficult to reach to your seat belt to strap in. In regards to the inbuilt tray / table, very difficult to use if you are above average height.

Seat 3J Diamond seats, my IFE not working, changing screens without any inputs. Restarted and same issues after restart. Brought to attention of flight attendant who witnessed issue 30min before Geneva. System restarted again in Geneva, same issues of non-functioning IFE throughout flight. What is the point of paying for business class if they do not provide something as simple as IFE? Even the review screen had errors on it.

In addition to the Long Haul and Untra Long Haul versions, Singapore Airlines operates a medium hall version of the A350 and that is by far my favourite. It offers the choice of either a left- or right-hand side consol. The seat configuration is 1-2-1 staggered. Each offers direct aisle access but for single seats with extra privacy choose A or K - 12, 15, 17, or 20. What makes these seats so great is they can be converted from upright to fully flatbed (and everything in between) with the push of a button. Unlike the other A350’s and 777’s with the crazy ‘flip’ seats that force you to sleep in a strange and uncomfortable angle. Regardless of where you sit, the seat offers a curved privacy wing with built in angle light options for reading. The 18″ screen provides access to the KrisWorld system which is loaded with movies, TV box seats, games and audio. You can control it by a touchscreen or use the remote which makes it easier to control the system while lying down. There is an AC power point and two high-speed USB charging ports in the console plus Business Class passengers can enjoy free Wi-Fi. There’s a blanket, large pillow, pair of slippers, eyeshades and a bottle of water at each seat. However, your unlikely to find an amenity kit, but these are available on demand.

Business class is just economy with an empty seat in the middle. At 188 cm tall, my knees hit the seat in front of me. When the passenger in front reclines the seat, it digs into my knees. And the flight is four hours. I don't recommend flying business class on this airline.

This is the worst economy seating I have been on,  the seats are very narrow and the seating hard. Having the back upright feels like you are being pushed froward, in recline they are just about tolerable. The leg room is very tight that cannot move your feet. There is no arm room and if you are in an aisle seat you are constantly being knocked by passengers and crew as they pass. The earphone socket was broken i had an 8hr flight with no entertainment.

Fantastic flight with Qatar Airways, the best I have flown. We were in economy class, but paid for an extra legroom seat. We were in a part of the aircraft with only 3 rows for a total of 24 seats, all with the same characteristics: a kind of Premium Economy. Due to the 2x4x2 configuration, the seats were very wide with enormous legroom and a very reclining backrest. I tried the Premium Economy of Singapore Airlines, but this flight of Qatar was much superior in terms of comfort.
No smooth boarding, very old cabin. Entertainment system outdated, very bad headphones provided. The food I wanted to select was already empty. Many scratches and dirt in seat environment.

This is the worst economy seating I have been on,  the seats are very narrow and the seating hard. Having the back upright feels like you are being pushed froward, in recline they are just about tolerable. The leg room is very tight that cannot move your feet. There is no arm room and if you are in an aisle seat you are constantly being knocked by passengers and crew as they pass. The earphone socket was broken i had an 8hr flight with no entertainment.

I would say I got given the worst seat on the plane even though there were other places available. Unusually for Tway meals and water was provided. However I found their service to still be most inadequate. The meal was just one box. The seat was supposed to come with a USB however just before take off the pilot said no USB was working. It would have been nice if they at least had the route map on display on one main screen for all passengers. What I also found displeasing is that though T'way is a no tv airline, they still had tv units installed. To make matters worse they still left the IFE control boxes installed. These were poorly located in the footwell area and took up half the space. Another awful feature of this flight was the underseat ambient lighting used when the main cabin lighting was dimmed. For some reason only my seat had a bright blue light under it which made it difficult to rest if my face had been angled downwards.

When booking on International flights with SAS Airbus A340/A330 aircraft. You have seat selection with your booking. Book 31 A and B (vice versa on other side of aircraft) which is near exit door. A lot of foot space and comfort.

CGY-MNL PR's domestic flights are great compared to there international flights. the seats were new and wide the legroom was great great staff and food. I didn't expect that they have TV screens although the show wasn't good but they have tv screens for a short flight.

I sat in the Premium Cabin on a long haul flight to Canada and the seats were appalling and did not justify extra expenditure. It was like sitting on a park bench and thankfully they supplied a blanket which I needed to sit on.

The aircraft seating was extremely cramped I am only 6' 1" yet I had to sit with my knees splayed apart even then both knees were against the back of the seat in front. My wife at 5' 5" felt most claustrophobic in one of the inner seats and thus spent most of the 8 hour flight standing. Not an aircraft to select on a long haul flight 2 hours at the outside would be more than enough to make most folk uncomfortable.

Plenty of legroom. No footrests on outbound but there was on return. Compared with most economy seats this was very good. Seats reclined to a comfortable position to sleep. All controls for entertainment easily accessible in front of you also screens tilt to suit your needs.

Danang to Saigon (Ho Chi Minh) was operated by an A330-300 leased from China Airlines. Economy seats were about 33" pitch with foot rests which lower from the seat in front of you and personal seat back video.
Very comfortable seats and excellent service so even though the flight was full we felt comfortable with the 12 hour flight from LAX to ICN (Incheon Korea).

I'm 6'2 and found the seat just bearable but luckily the seat in front didn't recline - if it had I would have been in trouble! Very difficult to get out of row though in flight. Cabin dirty with seat pocket filed with wet magazines and rubbish from earlier flight. Seat Back TVs faulty (both ways) as film kept jumping back 30 mins. Service OK but food poor even by airline standards

LAX-O'Hare on the oldest 767 I've flown on in many years. Filled with broken equipment - backseat pocket falling off overhead door would not shut etc. This plane was so old that it had 4 drop down 12" TV screens in center of plane for movies for 30+ rows of economy!

Overall the seats aren't too bad. I found that with a seat fully reclined you can hardly see the tv screen. Legroom space isn't too bad compared to many airlines I have flown and the seat width not too bad. Getting in and out of my seat was sometimes a pain in the neck since I tripped often due to the lack of space.

Seat was very tight on width and i am 6ft with a 34inch waist. Space was okay when forward seat was not reclined but when it was it felt very close and you could not read or use you table. In flight entertainment wasn't fully working either and they made no announcement about this. Seat head rest were poor.

ICN-TPE. There is no adjustable headrests and no personal television. There is a small overhead screen. The seats are clean however the tray table had leftover stain marks. There are foldable cup holders attached to the tray table. There is radio channels and complimentary ear phones are given for you to keep. The seats have no lumbar support. The recline is not very good (about 2 degrees).
LHR-NBO The flight was not full and there were plenty of free seats so I had a row of three to myself. If however I had been on a full flight I would have found it very cramped.
Above average comfort with fairly wide seat. Seat pitch still a problem for taller people though.

We were in seats 22 A and B (upper deck) but were fortunate enough not to have a third passenger in seat C giving us more room to spread out although I believe we would have been comfortable even with a third person. These seats are in the exit row so leg room is not an issue nor is the narrowness of the seats. I've heard complaints about the temperature but that wasn't a problem with the blankets provided. There really isn't much of a window for this row. The side storage bin is a little awkward to reach and can disturb the passenger behind you when accessing. Our return flight LHR to LAX – 747-400 – we had seats H and K in row 25. We found these seats to be extremely comfortable especially with no one behind us. Having the lavatory close by was not an issue most folks passing by were quiet.
The seats are very comfortable. Probably the most comfortable I ever flew with. It was a highly pleasant experience even it was only Economy. Can only recommend.

LHR-BKK-LHR. The legroom on Thai is excellent so much better than other airlines. Service is good and food is good. It makes the long flight so much more pleasant. Only downside is no seat back IFE - take your own if you can.

Very cramped and the headphone socket didn't work (attendant very offhand about it - said they knew 15 weren't working and so no point trying to reseat me). Shabby surroundings - seemed grubby and old.

When flying between Europe and Japan I prefer an aisle seat. So I changed from 14A to 22G. This was a major mistake as 22G has a large metal box directly adjacent to the anchor stays of the seat in front so it means that leg space for 22G is reduced by about half. Of course this does not appear on the seating chart at check-in but had I known this I would have stayed in 14A. That said I watched a film directly after the meal service (the second Narnia film) and then woke up just before breakfast. So I must have slept for about eight hours. Perhaps the Narnia film sent me to sleep or KLM's red wine served with dinner.

Delta's new seats on the Boeing 767-300 aircraft are terrible at best. They are extremely uncomfortable and aft of the overwing exit rows they are all misaligned with the windows. They do not have winged headrests and because the windows are misaligned you cannot rest your head on the wall next to you. Instead of typical recline the seatback reclines partially and the seat cushion slides forward which in reality offers less recline than typical economy seats. In addition the legroom is very poor except for the exit rows. All PTVs are touch screen so when the person behind you is using the system it can become very annoying as you feel the tapping throughout the flight.

I was sat in 8C. Being just over 2 metres tall there's barely a flight where the seat pitch is great enough (in economy) for me. The pitch was just about bearable and I could put my right leg out a little into the aisle during take-off so it was more comfortable. The crew were quite accommodating too once in the air they re-allocated me to 9H-J-K a vacant three-seater! Can't complain on that front I think 7 hours in that seat would've been too much to bear.

Row 13 C/D/E : paid for extra legroom which was excellent but there is a toilet on the right hand side and many travellers = cut across our seats from the left side. Cabin crew suggested we put our hand luggage on the floor as a mild deterrent - which did not work. Finally the crew chief put out a series of announcements telling people not to cross at row 13 and the other rows which had gaps - most people observed this firm request.

Euro Traveller OSL-LHR. After flying a lot of low-cost airlines this was a good experience. I had seat 6F with the middle seat empty. Would have felt a bit cramped with a full flight. However the seat width and legroom was good. Checked in online. Fast and easy.

The upper deck seating on the emergency exit row are highly desirable and usually only for their Global Club members. I was flying with a member so I could get it. They did block the middle seat and we had the aisle and window and the legroom is outrageously good. The problem is the width of the seat. It is probably 15" when you account for the IFE controller digging into your thigh the entire flight. Flew to the US in this same seat arrangement a few years back and it was equally miserable. Unless you are a typical Japanese size (small) this seat is horribly narrow. Don't know about legroom in the normal seats but it must be equally as bad.
Very old looking compared to Continental and Jetblue's cabins. Seats weren't too comfortable.

First time on LH and when I sat down I thought this was the most uncomfortable seat with the least legroom I had ever experienced. The seatback pockets were the smallest I had ever seen and when pulled out the table tray was on an forward incline. I had to stabilize it with one hand while I ate. When the passenger in front of me reclined his seat it was almost in my face. Because of this and as a courtesy to the passenger behind me I did not recline my seat throughout the whole YYZ-FRA flight.

Terrible seating experience. The most unconfortable seat I have ever been on. My feet kept on kicking a steel box that was located right where they were supposed to rest. So forget about putting anything underneath your front seat. I could hardly move on my 13-hour EZE-FRA (and back) flights. Very old ceiling mounted TVs provided terrible entertainment.

I got stuck in a bulkhead seat from DFW-EZE. I am 6'4" and 11 hours with no legroom to stretch out was torture. I had booked the seat behind mine (emergency exit row) but was given this seat at check-in and I failed to notice the change. Luckily it was relatively easy to climb past the aisle seat and get up and move around every hour or so. Miserable flight.

We have made several journeys in the upper cabin premium economy section. Not being in the least interested in business class the premium economy is an excellent alternative. However I do find the seat padding tends to set solid after about 8hours. I now have an additional cushion that that has largely eliminated this problem. Even double long haul legs ie LHR- HKG-AKL are good value and comfortable in these seats.

Seats 14j and 14K emergency exit seats. Very uncomfortable seats very narrow width very short seat belts. Only position you can only sit in is bolt upright with your arms folded for 6 or 7 hours due to space restriction rendering you unable to move in seat and lack of space between you and person next to you. Overall terrible seats and not worth the extra money.ar.
Overall the seat was okay but the seat recline was a disappointment.
The seats in twos at the rear of the aircraft are the more comfortable in economy.
Have flown Etihad many times and consider seats adequate or better. They should do away with footrests as they take up room for long legged passengers like myself even when not in use.

Flew to HKG from KCH via BWN on a mixture of A319 and A320. These RBA workhorses are beginning to show their age. Seats are very stiff and headrest keeps sliding down. Legroom and width was generous but not very comfortable to sleep in. Entertainment was the means of drop down screens. Got a stiff neck from trying to follow the movie. Food and service was excellent. Too Bad the seats were somewhat stiff.

Seats felt very cramped - worst I've ever experienced. Who is the genius that decided to put in new thickly padded and sculpted seats (which push you closer to the seat in front) with the most recline I've ever seen in Economy but kept the seat pitch at 31-32"? When the seat in front reclined the video screen was 8" in front of my face and it is impossible to reach the floor or stand up for that matter. It is ridiculously tight unless you are under 5'6".

I have travelled Premium Economy previously on an Air new Zealand 747.
